Here is a simple example which could be the URL definition for a blog::
from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule, NotFound, RequestRedirect
So what does that do?  First of all we create a new :class:`Map` which stores
a bunch of URL rules.  Then we pass it a list of :class:`Rule` objects.
Each :class:`Rule` object is instantiated with a string that represents a rule
and an endpoint which will be the alias for what view the rule represents.
Multiple rules can have the same endpoint, but should have different arguments
The format for the URL rules is straightforward, but explained in detail below.
Inside the WSGI application we bind the url_map to the current request which will
return a new :class:`MapAdapter`.  This url_map adapter can then be used to match
or build domains for the current request.
The :meth:`MapAdapter.match` method can then either return a tuple in the form
``(endpoint, args)`` or raise one of the three exceptions
or :exc:`~werkzeug.exceptions.RequestRedirect`.  For more details about those
exceptions have a look at the documentation of the :meth:`MapAdapter.match` method.
Rule strings are URL paths with placeholders for variable parts in the
(with parentheses) are optional. If no converter is given, the
``default`` converter is used (``string`` by default). The available
Rule path parts are separated by ``/`` and matched individually, unless a
converter opts in to matching ``/`` as well.
Rules that end with a slash are "branches", others are "leaves". If
``strict_slashes`` is enabled (the default), visiting a branch URL
without a trailing slash will redirect to the URL with a slash appended.
Many HTTP servers merge consecutive slashes into one when receiving
requests. If ``merge_slashes`` is enabled (the default), rules will
merge slashes in non-variable parts when matching and building. Visiting
a URL with consecutive slashes will redirect to the URL with slashes
merged. If you want to disable ``merge_slashes`` for a :class:`Rule` or
:class:`Map`, you'll also need to configure your web server
Besides the path, matching can also use the subdomain of a known base domain if
``subdomain_matching`` is enabled (the default), or the full host (if
``host_matching`` is enabled). The subdomain or host parts can also contain
variables. Unlike the path, where multiple parts are separated by ``/``, the
domain is always matched as a single part.
If a duplicate rule is added to a map, a :exc:`.DuplicateRuleError` will be
raised. Rules are compared based on their path, subdomain or host, websocket
mode, and methods. Variable parts are not equal if they use different
converters, although this heuristic may not be perfect depending on what the
different converters can actually match. Rules with equal or overlapping (but
not exactly equal) methods are considered duplicates. The ``HEAD`` and

62|        for filename in "/etc/machine-id", "/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id":
63|            try:

74|        # information. This is used outside containers too but should be
75|        # relatively stable across boots.
76|        try:
77|            with open("/proc/self/cgroup", "rb") as f:
78|                linux += f.readline().strip()
79|        except OSError:
80|            pass
81|
82|        if linux:
83|            return linux
84|
85|        # On OS X, use ioreg to get the computer's serial number.
86|        try:
87|            dump = subprocess.Popen(
88|                ["ioreg", "-c", "IOPlatformExpertDevice", "-d", "2"],
89|                stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
90|            ).communicate()[0]
91|            match = re.search(b'"serial-number" = <([^>]+)', dump)
92|
93|            if match is not None:
94|                return match.group(1)
95|        except OSError:
96|            pass
97|
98|        # On Windows, use winreg to get the machine guid.
99|        if sys.platform == "win32":
100|            import winreg
101|
102|            try:
103|                with winreg.OpenKey(
104|                    winreg.HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE,
105|                    "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Cryptography",
106|                    0,
107|                    winreg.KEY_READ | winreg.KEY_WOW64_64KEY,
108|                ) as rk:
109|                    guid: str | bytes
110|                    guid_type: int
111|                    guid, guid_type = winreg.QueryValueEx(rk, "MachineGuid")
112|
113|                    if guid_type == winreg.REG_SZ:
114|                        return guid.encode()
115|
116|                    return guid
117|            except OSError:
118|                pass
119|
120|        return None

139|def get_pin_and_cookie_name(
140|    app: wt.WSGIApplication,
141|) -> tuple[str, str] | tuple[None, None]:
142|    """Given an application object this returns a semi-stable 9 digit pin
143|    code and a random key.  The hope is that this is stable between
144|    restarts to not make debugging particularly frustrating.  If the pin
145|    was forcefully disabled this returns `None`.
146|
147|    Second item in the resulting tuple is the cookie name for remembering.
148|    """
149|    pin = os.environ.get("WERKZEUG_DEBUG_PIN")
150|    rv = None
151|    num = None
152|
153|    # Pin was explicitly disabled
154|    if pin == "off":
155|        return None, None
156|
157|    # Pin was provided explicitly
158|    if pin is not None and pin.replace("-", "").isdecimal():
159|        # If there are separators in the pin, return it directly
160|        if "-" in pin:
161|            rv = pin
162|        else:
163|            num = pin
164|
165|    modname = getattr(app, "__module__", t.cast(object, app).__class__.__module__)
166|    username: str | None
167|
168|    try:
169|        # Python < 3.13 may raise a KeyError if the UID does not have a
170|        # username, such as in Docker.
171|        username = getpass.getuser()
172|    except (KeyError, OSError):
173|        username = None
174|
175|    mod = sys.modules.get(modname)
176|
177|    # This information only exists to make the cookie unique on the
178|    # computer, not as a security feature.
179|    probably_public_bits = [
180|        username,
181|        modname,
182|        getattr(app, "__name__", type(app).__name__),
183|        getattr(mod, "__file__", None),
184|    ]
185|
186|    # This information is here to make it harder for an attacker to
187|    # guess the cookie name.  They are unlikely to be contained anywhere
188|    # within the unauthenticated debug page.
189|    private_bits = [str(uuid.getnode()), get_machine_id()]
190|
191|    h = hashlib.sha3_256()
192|    for bit in chain(probably_public_bits, private_bits):
193|        if not bit:
194|            continue
195|        if isinstance(bit, str):
196|            bit = bit.encode()
197|        h.update(bit)
198|    h.update(b"cookiesalt")
199|
200|    cookie_name = f"__wzd{h.hexdigest()[:20]}"
201|
202|    # If we need to generate a pin we salt it a bit more so that we don't
203|    # end up with the same value and generate out 9 digits
204|    if num is None:
205|        h.update(b"pinsalt")
206|        num = f"{int(h.hexdigest(), 16):09d}"[:9]
207|
208|    # Format the pincode in groups of digits for easier remembering if
209|    # we don't have a result yet.
210|    if rv is None:
211|        for group_size in 5, 4, 3:
212|            if len(num) % group_size == 0:
213|                rv = "-".join(
214|                    num[x : x + group_size].rjust(group_size, "0")
215|                    for x in range(0, len(num), group_size)
216|                )
217|                break
218|        else:
219|            rv = num
220|
221|    return rv, cookie_name

233|    state. Some state, such as context globals, cannot be restored with

329|    def debug_application(
330|        self, environ: wt.WSGIEnvironment, start_response: wt.StartResponse

332|        """Run the application and conserve the traceback frames."""

431|    def check_pin_trust(self, environ: wt.WSGIEnvironment) -> bool | None:

433|        request is trusted on a pin/cookie basis and returns `False` if not.
434|        Additionally if the cookie's stored pin hash is wrong it will return
435|        `None` so that appropriate action can be taken.

437|        if self.pin is None:
438|            return True
439|
440|        # If we failed too many times, then we're locked out.
441|        if self._failed_pin_auth.value >= 10:
442|            return False
443|
444|        val = parse_cookie(environ.get("HTTP_COOKIE")).get(self.pin_cookie_name)
445|        if not val or "|" not in val:
446|            return False
447|        ts_str, _, pin_hash = val.partition("|")

449|        try:
450|            ts = _plain_int(ts_str)
451|        except ValueError:
452|            return False
453|
454|        if pin_hash != hash_pin(self.pin):
455|            return None
456|        return (time.time() - PIN_TIME) < ts

468|    def pin_auth(self, request: Request) -> Response:

471|            return SecurityError()  # type: ignore[return-value]

475|        trust = self.check_pin_trust(request.environ)
476|        pin = t.cast(str, self.pin)

479|        # set but the stored pin hash value is bad.  This means that the
480|        # pin was changed.  In this case we count a bad auth and unset the
481|        # cookie.  This way it becomes harder to guess the cookie name
482|        # instead of the pin as we still count up failures.
483|        bad_cookie = False
484|        if trust is None:
485|            self._fail_pin_auth()

488|        # If we're trusted, we're authenticated.
489|        elif trust:
490|            auth = True
491|
492|        # If we failed too many times, then we're locked out.
493|        elif self._failed_pin_auth.value >= 10:
494|            exhausted = True
495|
496|        # Otherwise go through pin based authentication
497|        else:
498|            entered_pin = request.args["pin"]
499|
500|            if entered_pin.strip().replace("-", "") == pin.replace("-", ""):
501|                self._failed_pin_auth.value = 0

503|            else:
504|                self._fail_pin_auth()

506|        rv = Response(
507|            json.dumps({"auth": auth, "exhausted": exhausted}),

516|                secure=request.is_secure,

1|"""When it comes to combining multiple controller or view functions
2|(however you want to call them) you need a dispatcher. A simple way
3|would be applying regular expression tests on the ``PATH_INFO`` and
4|calling registered callback functions that return the value then.
5|
6|This module implements a much more powerful system than simple regular
7|expression matching because it can also convert values in the URLs and
8|build URLs.
9|
10|Here a simple example that creates a URL map for an application with
11|two subdomains (www and kb) and some URL rules:
12|
13|.. code-block:: python
14|
15|    m = Map([
16|        # Static URLs
17|        Rule('/', endpoint='static/index'),
18|        Rule('/about', endpoint='static/about'),
19|        Rule('/help', endpoint='static/help'),
20|        # Knowledge Base
21|        Subdomain('kb', [
22|            Rule('/', endpoint='kb/index'),
23|            Rule('/browse/', endpoint='kb/browse'),
24|            Rule('/browse/<int:id>/', endpoint='kb/browse'),
25|            Rule('/browse/<int:id>/<int:page>', endpoint='kb/browse')
26|        ])
27|    ], default_subdomain='www')
28|
29|If the application doesn't use subdomains it's perfectly fine to not set
30|the default subdomain and not use the `Subdomain` rule factory. The
31|endpoint in the rules can be anything, for example import paths or
32|unique identifiers. The WSGI application can use those endpoints to get the
33|handler for that URL.  It doesn't have to be a string at all but it's
34|recommended.
35|
36|Now it's possible to create a URL adapter for one of the subdomains and
37|build URLs:
38|
39|.. code-block:: python
40|
41|    c = m.bind('example.com')
42|
43|    c.build("kb/browse", dict(id=42))
44|    'http://kb.example.com/browse/42/'
45|
46|    c.build("kb/browse", dict())
47|    'http://kb.example.com/browse/'
48|
49|    c.build("kb/browse", dict(id=42, page=3))
50|    'http://kb.example.com/browse/42/3'
51|
52|    c.build("static/about")
53|    '/about'
54|
55|    c.build("static/index", force_external=True)
56|    'http://www.example.com/'
57|
58|    c = m.bind('example.com', subdomain='kb')
59|
60|    c.build("static/about")
61|    'http://www.example.com/about'
62|
63|The first argument to bind is the server name *without* the subdomain.
64|Per default it will assume that the script is mounted on the root, but
65|often that's not the case so you can provide the real mount point as
66|second argument:
67|
68|.. code-block:: python
69|
70|    c = m.bind('example.com', '/applications/example')
71|
72|The third argument can be the subdomain, if not given the default
73|subdomain is used.  For more details about binding have a look at the
74|documentation of the `MapAdapter`.
75|
76|And here is how you can match URLs:
77|
78|.. code-block:: python
79|
80|    c = m.bind('example.com')
81|
82|    c.match("/")
83|    ('static/index', {})
84|
85|    c.match("/about")
86|    ('static/about', {})
87|
88|    c = m.bind('example.com', '/', 'kb')
89|
90|    c.match("/")
91|    ('kb/index', {})
92|
93|    c.match("/browse/42/23")
94|    ('kb/browse', {'id': 42, 'page': 23})
95|
96|If matching fails you get a ``NotFound`` exception, if the rule thinks
97|it's a good idea to redirect (for example because the URL was defined
98|to have a slash at the end but the request was missing that slash) it
99|will raise a ``RequestRedirect`` exception. Both are subclasses of
100|``HTTPException`` so you can use those errors as responses in the
101|application.
102|
103|If matching succeeded but the URL rule was incompatible to the given
104|method (for example there were only rules for ``GET`` and ``HEAD`` but
105|routing tried to match a ``POST`` request) a ``MethodNotAllowed``
106|exception is raised.
107|"""

158|def _get_input_stream(
159|    environ: wt.WSGIEnvironment,

161|    max_content_length: int | None = None,

166|    functions, which are not responsible for enforcing this limit.

169|    :exc:`RequestEntityTooLarge`` ``413 Content Too Large`` error is raised.

172|    server handles terminating the stream, so it is safe to read directly. For example,
173|    a server that knows how to handle chunked requests safely would set this.
174|

176|    ``wsgi.input_terminated`` is set. Otherwise, an empty stream is returned unless the
177|    user explicitly disables this safe fallback.

180|    that is too large, or an infinite stream), the remaining contents of the stream
181|    cannot be read safely. Depending on how the server handles this, clients may show a
182|    "connection reset" failure instead of seeing the 413 response.

185|    :param safe_fallback: Return an empty stream when ``Content-Length`` is not set.

187|    :param max_content_length: The maximum length that content-length or streaming
188|        requests may not exceed.

192|
193|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3.2

195|        ``wsgi.input_terminated``.

197|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3

199|
200|    .. versionadded:: 0.9

202|    from .wrappers.request import Request
203|

205|    request.max_content_length = max_content_length

209|        not safe_fallback
210|        and isinstance(stream, io.BytesIO)

234|class ClosingIterator:
235|    """Wrap an iterable that may or may not have a ``close`` method, adding that
236|    and additional functions to its own ``close`` method.
237|
238|    Rather than using this directly, build a :class:`.Response` and use its
239|    :meth:`~.Response.call_on_close` method to add cleanup functions. It will
240|    handle creating the closing iterator.
241|
242|    If a WSGI application returns an iterable with a ``close`` method, it
243|    will be called by the server at the end of the response. This class can be
244|    used to add additional cleanup when receiving an iterable from some other
245|    code.
246|
247|    This does not handle the case where an exception interrupts the application
248|    before it returns the iterable. A higher level wrapper to handle safe
249|    execution and resource cleanup is needed.
250|    """
251|
252|    def __init__(
253|        self,
254|        iterable: t.Iterable[bytes],
255|        callbacks: t.Callable[[], None]
256|        | t.Iterable[t.Callable[[], None]]
257|        | None = None,
258|    ) -> None:
259|        iterator = iter(iterable)
260|        self._next = t.cast(t.Callable[[], bytes], partial(next, iterator))
261|        if callbacks is None:
262|            callbacks = []
263|        elif callable(callbacks):
264|            callbacks = [callbacks]
265|        else:
266|            callbacks = list(callbacks)
267|        iterable_close = getattr(iterable, "close", None)
268|        if iterable_close:
269|            callbacks.insert(0, iterable_close)
270|        self._callbacks = callbacks
271|
272|    def __iter__(self) -> ClosingIterator:
273|        return self
274|
275|    def __next__(self) -> bytes:
276|        return self._next()
277|
278|    def close(self) -> None:
279|        for callback in self._callbacks:
280|            callback()

349|class _RangeWrapper:
350|    """This class can be used to convert an iterable object into
351|    an iterable that will only yield a piece of the underlying content.
352|    It yields blocks until the underlying stream range is fully read.
353|    The yielded blocks will have a size that can't exceed the original
354|    iterator defined block size, but that can be smaller.
355|
356|    If you're using this object together with a :class:`Response` you have
357|    to use the `direct_passthrough` mode.
358|
359|    :param iterable: an iterable object with a :meth:`__next__` method.
360|    :param start_byte: byte from which read will start.
361|    :param byte_range: how many bytes to read.
362|    """
363|
364|    def __init__(
365|        self,
366|        iterable: t.Iterable[bytes] | t.IO[bytes],
367|        start_byte: int = 0,
368|        byte_range: int | None = None,
369|    ):
370|        self.iterable = iter(iterable)
371|        self.byte_range = byte_range
372|        self.start_byte = start_byte
373|        self.end_byte = None
374|
375|        if byte_range is not None:
376|            self.end_byte = start_byte + byte_range
377|
378|        self.read_length = 0
379|        self.seekable = hasattr(iterable, "seekable") and iterable.seekable()
380|        self.end_reached = False
381|
382|    def __iter__(self) -> _RangeWrapper:
383|        return self
384|
385|    def _next_chunk(self) -> bytes:
386|        try:
387|            chunk = next(self.iterable)
388|            self.read_length += len(chunk)
389|            return chunk
390|        except StopIteration:
391|            self.end_reached = True
392|            raise
393|
394|    def _first_iteration(self) -> tuple[bytes | None, int]:
395|        chunk = None
396|        if self.seekable:
397|            self.iterable.seek(self.start_byte)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
398|            self.read_length = self.iterable.tell()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
399|            contextual_read_length = self.read_length
400|        else:
401|            while self.read_length <= self.start_byte:
402|                chunk = self._next_chunk()
403|            if chunk is not None:
404|                chunk = chunk[self.start_byte - self.read_length :]
405|            contextual_read_length = self.start_byte
406|        return chunk, contextual_read_length
407|
408|    def _next(self) -> bytes:
409|        if self.end_reached:
410|            raise StopIteration()
411|        chunk = None
412|        contextual_read_length = self.read_length
413|        if self.read_length == 0:
414|            chunk, contextual_read_length = self._first_iteration()
415|        if chunk is None:
416|            chunk = self._next_chunk()
417|        if self.end_byte is not None and self.read_length >= self.end_byte:
418|            self.end_reached = True
419|            return chunk[: self.end_byte - contextual_read_length]
420|        return chunk
421|
422|    def __next__(self) -> bytes:
423|        chunk = self._next()
424|        if chunk:
425|            return chunk
426|        self.end_reached = True
427|        raise StopIteration()
428|
429|    def close(self) -> None:
430|        if hasattr(self.iterable, "close"):
431|            self.iterable.close()

434|class _LimitedStream(io.RawIOBase):
435|    """Wrap a stream so that it doesn't read more than a given limit. This is
436|    used to limit ``wsgi.input`` to the ``Content-Length`` header value or
437|    :attr:`.Request.max_content_length`.
438|

440|    file that is too large, or an infinite stream), the remaining contents of
441|    the stream cannot be read safely. Depending on how the server handles this,
442|    clients may show a "connection reset" failure instead of seeing the 413
443|    response.
444|
445|    :param stream: The stream to read from. Must be a readable binary IO object.
446|    :param limit: The limit in bytes to not read past. Should be either the
447|        ``Content-Length`` header value or ``request.max_content_length``.
448|    :param is_max: Whether the given ``limit`` is ``request.max_content_length``
449|        instead of the ``Content-Length`` header value. This changes how
450|        exhausted and disconnect events are handled.
451|    :raises .RequestEntityTooLarge: Attempted to read after a max limit.
452|    :raises .ClientDisconnected: Reading returned zero bytes or raised an error,
453|        when the limit is not a max.

456|        Will be private in Werkzeug 4.0. Use ``Request.stream`` instead.

462|        Implements ``io.RawIOBase`` rather than ``io.IOBase``.
463|    """
464|
465|    def __init__(self, stream: t.IO[bytes], limit: int, is_max: bool = False) -> None:
466|        self._stream = stream
467|        self._pos = 0
468|        self.limit = limit
469|        self._limit_is_max = is_max
470|
471|    @property
472|    def is_exhausted(self) -> bool:
473|        """Whether the current stream position has reached the limit."""
474|        return self._pos >= self.limit

476|    def on_exhausted(self) -> None:
477|        """Called when attempting to read after the limit has been reached. If
478|        the limit is a maximum, raises :exc:`.RequestEntityTooLarge`.
479|
480|        .. versionchanged:: 2.3
481|            Raises ``RequestEntityTooLarge`` if the limit is a maximum.
482|
483|        .. versionchanged:: 2.3
484|            Any return value is ignored.
485|        """
486|        if self._limit_is_max:
487|            raise RequestEntityTooLarge()

489|    def on_disconnect(self, error: Exception | None = None) -> None:
490|        """Called when an attempted read receives zero bytes before the limit
491|        was reached. This indicates that the client disconnected before sending
492|        the full request body. Raises :exc:`.ClientDisconnected`, unless the
493|        limit is a maximum and no error was raised.
494|
495|        .. versionchanged:: 2.3
496|            Added the ``error`` parameter. Do nothing if the limit is a maximum and no
497|            error was raised.
498|
499|        .. versionchanged:: 2.3
500|            Any return value is ignored.
501|        """

503|            raise ClientDisconnected()
504|

506|        # streaming body is complete. There's no way to distinguish that from the

527|    def readinto(self, b: bytearray) -> int | None:  # type: ignore[override]
528|        size = len(b)

530|
531|        if remaining <= 0:
532|            self.on_exhausted()
533|            return 0
534|
535|        if hasattr(self._stream, "readinto"):
536|            # Use stream.readinto if it's available.
537|            if size <= remaining:
538|                # The size fits in the remaining limit, use the buffer directly.
539|                try:
540|                    out_size: int | None = self._stream.readinto(b)
541|                except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
542|                    self.on_disconnect(error=e)
543|                    return 0
544|            else:
545|                # Use a temp buffer with the remaining limit as the size.
546|                temp_b = bytearray(remaining)
547|
548|                try:
549|                    out_size = self._stream.readinto(temp_b)
550|                except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
551|                    self.on_disconnect(error=e)
552|                    return 0
553|
554|                if out_size:

556|                    # size=10, remaining=5, out_size=3, remaining > out_size

573|            self.on_disconnect()
574|            return 0

579|    def readall(self) -> bytes:
580|        if self.is_exhausted:

586|        # The parent implementation uses "while True", which results in an extra read.
587|        while not self.is_exhausted:

591|            if not data:

192|def quote_header_value(value: t.Any, allow_token: bool = True) -> str:
193|    """Add double quotes around a header value. If the header contains only ASCII token
194|    characters, it will be returned unchanged. If the header contains ``"`` or ``\\``
195|    characters, they will be escaped with an additional ``\\`` character.
196|
197|    This is the reverse of :func:`unquote_header_value`.
198|
199|    :param value: The value to quote. Will be converted to a string.
200|    :param allow_token: Disable to quote the value even if it only has token characters.
201|
202|    .. versionchanged:: 3.0
203|        Passing bytes is not supported.
204|
205|    .. versionchanged:: 3.0
206|        The ``extra_chars`` parameter is removed.
207|
208|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3
209|        The value is quoted if it is the empty string.
210|
211|    .. versionadded:: 0.5
212|    """
213|    value_str = str(value)
214|
215|    if not value_str:
216|        return '""'
217|
218|    if allow_token:
219|        token_chars = _token_chars
220|
221|        if token_chars.issuperset(value_str):
222|            return value_str
223|
224|    value_str = value_str.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
225|    return f'"{value_str}"'

250|def dump_options_header(header: str | None, options: t.Mapping[str, t.Any]) -> str:
251|    """Produce a header value and ``key=value`` parameters separated by semicolons
252|    ``;``. For example, the ``Content-Type`` header.
253|
254|    .. code-block:: python
255|
256|        dump_options_header("text/html", {"charset": "UTF-8"})
257|        'text/html; charset=UTF-8'
258|
259|    This is the reverse of :func:`parse_options_header`.
260|
261|    If a value contains non-token characters, it will be quoted.
262|
263|    If a value is ``None``, the parameter is skipped.
264|
265|    In some keys for some headers, a UTF-8 value can be encoded using a special
266|    ``key*=UTF-8''value`` form, where ``value`` is percent encoded. This function will
267|    not produce that format automatically, but if a given key ends with an asterisk
268|    ``*``, the value is assumed to have that form and will not be quoted further.
269|
270|    :param header: The primary header value.
271|    :param options: Parameters to encode as ``key=value`` pairs.
272|
273|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3
274|        Keys with ``None`` values are skipped rather than treated as a bare key.
275|
276|    .. versionchanged:: 2.2.3
277|        If a key ends with ``*``, its value will not be quoted.
278|    """
279|    segments = []
280|
281|    if header is not None:
282|        segments.append(header)
283|
284|    for key, value in options.items():
285|        if value is None:
286|            continue
287|
288|        if key.endswith("*"):
289|            segments.append(f"{key}={value}")
290|        else:
291|            segments.append(f"{key}={quote_header_value(value)}")
292|
293|    return "; ".join(segments)

301|    :func:`parse_set_header`.

308|    ``key*=UTF-8''value`` form, where ``value`` is percent encoded. This function will
309|    not produce that format automatically, but if a given key ends with an asterisk
310|    ``*``, the value is assumed to have that form and will not be quoted further.
311|

313|
314|        dump_header(["foo", "bar baz"])

323|        The ``allow_token`` parameter is removed.
324|
325|    .. versionchanged:: 2.2.3
326|        If a key ends with ``*``, its value will not be quoted.
327|    """
328|    if isinstance(iterable, cabc.Mapping):
329|        items = []
330|
331|        for key, value in iterable.items():
332|            if value is None:
333|                items.append(key)
334|            elif key.endswith("*"):
335|                items.append(f"{key}={value}")
336|            else:
337|                items.append(f"{key}={quote_header_value(value)}")
338|    else:

361|def parse_list_header(value: str) -> list[str]:
362|    """Parse a header value that consists of a list of comma separated items according
363|    to `RFC 9110 <https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#abnf.extension>`__.
364|
365|    Surrounding quotes are removed from items, but internal quotes are left for
366|    future parsing. Empty values are discarded.
367|
368|    .. code-block:: python
369|
370|        parse_list_header('token, "quoted value"')
371|        ['token', 'quoted value']
372|
373|    This is the reverse of :func:`dump_header`.
374|
375|    :param value: The header value to parse.
376|
377|    .. versionchanged:: 3.2
378|        Quotes and escapes are kept if only part of an item is quoted. Empty
379|        values are omitted. An empty list is returned if the value contains an
380|        unclosed quoted string.
381|    """
382|    items = []
383|    item = ""
384|    escape = False
385|    quote = False
386|
387|    for char in value:
388|        if escape:
389|            escape = False
390|            item += char
391|            continue
392|
393|        if quote:
394|            if char == "\\":
395|                escape = True
396|            elif char == '"':
397|                quote = False
398|
399|            item += char
400|            continue
401|
402|        if char == ",":
403|            items.append(item)
404|            item = ""
405|            continue
406|
407|        if char == '"':
408|            quote = True
409|
410|        item += char
411|
412|    if quote:
413|        # invalid, unclosed quoted string
414|        return []
415|
416|    items.append(item)
417|    return [
418|        unquote_header_value(item)
419|        for item in (item.strip(" \t") for item in items)
420|        if item
421|    ]

424|def parse_dict_header(value: str) -> dict[str, str | None]:
425|    """Parse a list header using :func:`parse_list_header`, then parse each item as a
426|    ``key=value`` pair.
427|
428|    .. code-block:: python
429|
430|        parse_dict_header('a=b, c="d, e", f')
431|        {"a": "b", "c": "d, e", "f": None}
432|
433|    This is the reverse of :func:`dump_header`.
434|
435|    If a key does not have a value, it is ``None``.
436|
437|    This handles charsets for values as described in
438|    `RFC 2231 <https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2231#section-3>`__. Only ASCII, UTF-8,
439|    and ISO-8859-1 charsets are accepted, otherwise the value remains quoted.
440|
441|    :param value: The header value to parse.
442|
443|    .. versionchanged:: 3.2
444|        An empty dict is returned if the value contains an unclosed quoted
445|        string.
446|
447|    .. versionchanged:: 3.0
448|        Passing bytes is not supported.
449|
450|    .. versionchanged:: 3.0
451|        The ``cls`` argument is removed.
452|
453|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3
454|        Added support for ``key*=charset''value`` encoded items.
455|
456|    .. versionchanged:: 0.9
457|       The ``cls`` argument was added.
458|    """
459|    result: dict[str, str | None] = {}
460|
461|    for item in parse_list_header(value):
462|        key, has_value, value = item.partition("=")
463|        key = key.strip(" \t")
464|
465|        if not key:
466|            # =value is not valid
467|            continue
468|
469|        if not has_value:
470|            result[key] = None
471|            continue
472|
473|        value = value.strip(" \t")
474|        encoding: str | None = None
475|
476|        if key.endswith("*"):
477|            # key*=charset''value becomes key=value, where value is percent encoded
478|            # adapted from parse_options_header, without the continuation handling
479|            key = key[:-1]
480|
481|            if (m_charset := _charset_value_re.match(value)) is not None:
482|                # If there is a charset marker in the value, split it off.
483|                encoding, value = m_charset.groups()
484|                encoding = encoding.lower()
485|
486|            # A safe list of encodings. Modern clients should only send ASCII or UTF-8.
487|            # This list will not be extended further. An invalid encoding will leave the

515|def parse_options_header(value: str | None) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]]:
516|    """Parse a header that consists of a value with ``key=value`` parameters separated
517|    by semicolons ``;``. For example, the ``Content-Type`` header.
518|
519|    .. code-block:: python
520|
521|        parse_options_header("text/html; charset=UTF-8")
522|        ('text/html', {'charset': 'UTF-8'})
523|
524|        parse_options_header("")
525|        ("", {})
526|
527|    This is the reverse of :func:`dump_options_header`.
528|
529|    This parses valid parameter parts as described in
530|    `RFC 9110 <https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#parameter>`__. Invalid parts are
531|    skipped.
532|
533|    This handles continuations and charsets as described in
534|    `RFC 2231 <https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2231#section-3>`__, although not as
535|    strictly as the RFC. Only ASCII, UTF-8, and ISO-8859-1 charsets are accepted,
536|    otherwise the value remains quoted.
537|
538|    Clients may not be consistent in how they handle a quote character within a quoted
539|    value. The `HTML Standard <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#multipart-form-data>`__
540|    replaces it with ``%22`` in multipart form data.
541|    `RFC 9110 <https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#quoted.strings>`__ uses backslash
542|    escapes in HTTP headers. Both are decoded to the ``"`` character.
543|
544|    Clients may not be consistent in how they handle non-ASCII characters. HTML
545|    documents must declare ``<meta charset=UTF-8>``, otherwise browsers may replace with
546|    HTML character references, which can be decoded using :func:`html.unescape`.
547|
548|    :param value: The header value to parse.
549|    :return: ``(value, options)``, where ``options`` is a dict
550|
551|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3
552|        Invalid parts, such as keys with no value, quoted keys, and incorrectly quoted
553|        values, are discarded instead of treating as ``None``.
554|
555|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3
556|        Only ASCII, UTF-8, and ISO-8859-1 are accepted for charset values.
557|
558|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3
559|        Escaped quotes in quoted values, like ``%22`` and ``\\"``, are handled.
560|
561|    .. versionchanged:: 2.2
562|        Option names are always converted to lowercase.
563|
564|    .. versionchanged:: 2.2

566|
567|    .. versionchanged:: 0.15
568|        :rfc:`2231` parameter continuations are handled.
569|
570|    .. versionadded:: 0.5
571|    """

573|        return "", {}

575|    value, _, rest = value.partition(";")

577|    rest = rest.strip(" \t")

580|        # empty (invalid) value, or value without options
581|        return value, {}
582|
583|    # Collect all valid key=value parts without processing the value.
584|    parts: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
585|    scan_pos = 0
586|    length = len(rest)
587|
588|    while scan_pos < length:
589|        if (m_key := _parameter_key_re.match(rest, scan_pos)) is not None:
590|            pk = m_key.group(1).lower()

594|            if (m_value := _parameter_token_value_re.match(rest, scan_pos)) is not None:
595|                parts.append((pk, m_value.group()))

598|            elif rest.startswith('"', scan_pos):

600|
601|                while quote_pos < length:
602|                    if rest.startswith(("\\\\", '\\"'), quote_pos):
603|                        # Consume escaped slashes and quotes.
604|                        quote_pos += 2
605|                    elif rest.startswith('"', quote_pos):
606|                        # Stop at an unescaped quote.
607|                        quote_pos += 1
608|                        parts.append((pk, rest[scan_pos:quote_pos]))
609|                        scan_pos = quote_pos
610|                        break

613|                        quote_pos += 1
614|                else:

616|                    break

619|        if m_delim := _parameter_delimiter_re.search(rest, scan_pos):
620|            scan_pos = m_delim.end()

625|    continuations: dict[str, list[str]] = {}

627|

629|    # unquote quoted values.

637|        ) is not None and m_mark.end() - m_mark.start() > 0:

643|        if has_charset:

645|                # If there is a valid charset marker in the value, split it off.
646|                encoding, pv = m_charset.groups()

648|                encoding = encoding.lower()

651|            if not encoding and has_continuation:
652|                encoding = continuation_encodings.get(pk)
653|

655|            # This list will not be extended further. An invalid encoding will leave the
656|            # value quoted.
657|            if encoding in {"ascii", "us-ascii", "utf-8", "iso-8859-1"}:

662|            # percent-encoded quotes.
663|            pv = unquote_header_value(pv).replace("%22", '"')

666|        if has_continuation:
667|            # Remove prior normal option.
668|            if pk in options:
669|                del options[pk]

672|            # sequential numbering.
673|            if pk in continuations:

675|            else:

679|            if encoding:

682|            # Remove prior continuation option.
683|            if pk in continuations:
684|                del continuations[pk]

687|            options[pk] = pv

148|    gain access to the other values, too, you have to use the `list` methods as
149|    explained below.

155|    MultiDict([('a', 'b'), ('a', 'c')])

164|    first value when multiple values for one key are found.

167|    subclass of the :exc:`~exceptions.BadRequest` HTTP exception and will
168|    render a page for a ``400 BAD REQUEST`` if caught in a catch-all for HTTP
169|    exceptions.

172|    ``(key, value)`` tuples, a dict, a :class:`MultiDict` or from Werkzeug 0.2

211|def redirect(
212|    location: str, code: int = 303, Response: type[Response] | None = None
213|) -> Response:
214|    """Create a response that redirects the client to the target location.
215|

217|    ``GET`` request to the target, regardless of what method the current request
218|    is. This produces the correct result for the common use cases: page redirects
219|    and form success. The status codes you're likely to use are:
220|
221|    -   ``303 See Other`` always uses a ``GET`` request.
222|    -   ``307 Temporary Redirect`` preserves the current method.
223|    -   ``308 Permanent Redirect`` preserves the current method, and instructs
224|        the client to permanently apply the result. This is hard to undo once
225|        you've sent it, so be sure the permanence is what you want.
226|
227|    Two older codes, ``302 Found`` and ``301 Moved Permanently``, are
228|    superseded by ``307`` and ``308`` respectively. They were not consistently
229|    implemented by clients, which tend to switch ``POST`` to ``GET`` but
230|    preserve other methods. Prefer using ``303``, ``307``, and ``308`` to get
231|    the exact behavior you intend. Other ``3xx`` codes are either not defined or
232|    have specific use cases.
233|
234|    :param location: The URL to redirect to. The client will interpret a
235|        relative URL (without the host) as relative to the host it's accessing.
236|    :param code: The redirect status code. This affects how the client issues
237|        the next request. Defaults to ``303``.

239|        :class:`werkzeug.wrappers.Response`.

242|        ``code`` defaults to 303 instead of 302.
243|
244|    .. versionchanged:: 0.10
245|        Added the ``response`` parameter.
246|
247|    .. versionchanged:: 0.6
248|        ``location`` can contain Unicode characters.
249|    """
250|    if Response is None:
251|        from .wrappers import Response
252|
253|    html_location = escape(location)
254|    response = Response(  # type: ignore[misc]
255|        "<!doctype html>\n"
256|        "<html lang=en>\n"
257|        "<title>Redirecting...</title>\n"
258|        "<h1>Redirecting...</h1>\n"
259|        "<p>You should be redirected automatically to the target URL: "
260|        f'<a href="{html_location}">{html_location}</a>. If not, click the link.\n',

269|    """Redirect to the current URL with a slash appended.
270|

272|    ``42/``. When joined to the current URL during response
273|    processing or by the browser, this will produce ``/user/42/``.

276|    called unconditionally on a URL, it may produce a redirect loop.

284|        ``strict_slashes`` instead.

288|        Relevant when the current path has multiple segments.

290|    .. versionchanged:: 2.1

292|        the request method and body.

294|    tail = environ["PATH_INFO"].rpartition("/")[2]

296|    if not tail:

299|        new_path = f"{tail}/"

557|def send_from_directory(
558|    directory: os.PathLike[str] | str,
559|    path: os.PathLike[str] | str,
560|    environ: wt.WSGIEnvironment,
561|    **kwargs: t.Any,
562|) -> Response:
563|    """Send a file from within a directory using :func:`send_file`.
564|
565|    This is a secure way to serve files from a folder, such as static
566|    files or uploads. Uses :func:`~werkzeug.security.safe_join` to
567|    ensure the path coming from the client is not maliciously crafted to
568|    point outside the specified directory.

570|    If the final path does not point to an existing regular file,
571|    returns a 404 :exc:`~werkzeug.exceptions.NotFound` error.
572|
573|    :param directory: The directory that ``path`` must be located under. This *must not*
574|        be a value provided by the client, otherwise it becomes insecure.
575|    :param path: The path to the file to send, relative to ``directory``. This is the
576|        part of the path provided by the client, which is checked for security.
577|    :param environ: The WSGI environ for the current request.
578|    :param kwargs: Arguments to pass to :func:`send_file`.
579|
580|    .. versionadded:: 2.0
581|        Adapted from Flask's implementation.
582|    """
583|    path_str = safe_join(os.fspath(directory), os.fspath(path))
584|
585|    if path_str is None:
586|        raise NotFound()
587|
588|    # Flask will pass app.root_path, allowing its send_from_directory
589|    # wrapper to not have to deal with paths.
590|    if "_root_path" in kwargs:

592|
593|    if not os.path.isfile(path_str):
594|        raise NotFound()
595|
596|    return send_file(path_str, environ, **kwargs)

599|def import_string(import_name: str, silent: bool = False) -> t.Any:
600|    """Imports an object based on a string.  This is useful if you want to
601|    use import paths as endpoints or something similar.  An import path can
602|    be specified either in dotted notation (``xml.sax.saxutils.escape``)
603|    or with a colon as object delimiter (``xml.sax.saxutils:escape``).
604|
605|    If `silent` is True the return value will be `None` if the import fails.
606|
607|    :param import_name: the dotted name for the object to import.
608|    :param silent: if set to `True` import errors are ignored and
609|                   `None` is returned instead.
610|    :return: imported object
611|    """
612|    import_name = import_name.replace(":", ".")
613|    try:
614|        try:
615|            __import__(import_name)
616|        except ImportError:
617|            if "." not in import_name:
618|                raise
619|        else:
620|            return sys.modules[import_name]
621|
622|        module_name, obj_name = import_name.rsplit(".", 1)
623|        module = __import__(module_name, globals(), locals(), [obj_name])
624|        try:
625|            return getattr(module, obj_name)
626|        except AttributeError as e:
627|            raise ImportError(e) from None
628|
629|    except ImportError as e:
630|        if not silent:
631|            raise ImportStringError(import_name, e).with_traceback(
632|                sys.exc_info()[2]
633|            ) from None
634|
635|    return None

638|def find_modules(
639|    import_path: str, include_packages: bool = False, recursive: bool = False
640|) -> t.Iterator[str]:
641|    """Finds all the modules below a package.  This can be useful to
642|    automatically import all views / controllers so that their metaclasses /
643|    function decorators have a chance to register themselves on the
644|    application.
645|
646|    Packages are not returned unless `include_packages` is `True`.  This can
647|    also recursively list modules but in that case it will import all the
648|    packages to get the correct load path of that module.
649|
650|    :param import_path: the dotted name for the package to find child modules.
651|    :param include_packages: set to `True` if packages should be returned, too.
652|    :param recursive: set to `True` if recursion should happen.
653|    :return: generator
654|    """
655|    module = import_string(import_path)
656|    path = getattr(module, "__path__", None)
657|    if path is None:
658|        raise ValueError(f"{import_path!r} is not a package")
659|    basename = f"{module.__name__}."
660|    for _importer, modname, ispkg in pkgutil.iter_modules(path):
661|        modname = basename + modname
662|        if ispkg:
663|            if include_packages:
664|                yield modname
665|            if recursive:
666|                yield from find_modules(modname, include_packages, True)
667|        else:
668|            yield modname

671|class ImportStringError(ImportError):
672|    """Provides information about a failed :func:`import_string` attempt."""
673|
674|    #: String in dotted notation that failed to be imported.
675|    import_name: str
676|    #: Wrapped exception.
677|    exception: BaseException
678|
679|    def __init__(self, import_name: str, exception: BaseException) -> None:
680|        self.import_name = import_name
681|        self.exception = exception
682|        msg = import_name
683|        name = ""
684|        tracked = []

687|            imported = import_string(name, silent=True)
688|            if imported:

690|            else:
691|                track = [f"- {n!r} found in {i!r}." for n, i in tracked]
692|                track.append(f"- {name!r} not found.")

696|                    f" are:\n\n"
697|                    "- missing __init__.py in a package;\n"
698|                    "- package or module path not included in sys.path;\n"
699|                    "- duplicated package or module name taking precedence in"
700|                    " sys.path;\n"
701|                    "- missing module, class, function or variable;\n\n"
702|                    f"Debugged import:\n\n{track_str}\n\n"
703|                    f"Original exception:\n\n{type(exception).__name__}: {exception}"
704|                )

227|            # Allow either a function (environ, start_response) or a
228|            # bound method (self, environ, start_response).

503|    @cached_property
504|    def stream(self) -> t.IO[bytes]:

506|        past the ``Content-Length`` header or :attr:`max_content_length`.
507|
508|        Use :meth:`get_data` to get the full data as bytes or text. The
509|        :attr:`data` attribute will contain the full bytes only if they do not
510|        represent form data. The :attr:`form` and :attr:`files` attributes will
511|        contain the parsed form data in that case.

514|        be checked immediately, or if that's not set the stream will be limited
515|        to ``Content-Length``. If the client does not send ``Content-Length``,
516|        it is not safe to read and an empty stream is returned.
517|
518|        However, the WSGI server can set ``environ["wsgi.input_terminated"]`` to
519|        indicate that it handles input without ``Content-Length``, such as by
520|        using non-blocking reads, buffering, and termination. This does not mean
521|        the stream might not be infinite, only that it is now safe to read.
522|        Therefore, you should still set :attr:`max_content_length`.
523|
524|        If the limit is reached before the underlying stream is exhausted, its
525|        remaining content cannot be read safely. Depending on how the server
526|        handles this, clients may show a "connection reset" failure instead of
527|        seeing the 413 response.
528|
529|        :raise .RequestEntityTooLarge: If :attr:`max_content_length` is exceeded.
530|
531|        .. versionchanged:: 2.3.2
532|            ``max_content_length`` is only applied to requests if the server
533|            sets ``wsgi.input_terminated``.
534|
535|        .. versionchanged:: 2.3
536|            Check ``max_content_length`` preemptively and while reading.
537|
538|        .. versionchanged:: 0.9
539|            The stream remains available (but consumed) if form parsing was
540|            accessed first.

543|            raise RuntimeError(
544|                "This request was created with 'shallow=True', reading"
545|                " from the input stream is disabled."
546|            )
547|
548|        stream: t.IO[bytes] = self.environ["wsgi.input"]
549|
550|        if (
551|            self.content_length is not None
552|            and self.max_content_length is not None
553|            and self.content_length > self.max_content_length
554|        ):
555|            raise RequestEntityTooLarge()
556|
557|        # A WSGI server can set this to indicate that it terminates the input
558|        # stream. In that case the stream is safe without wrapping, or can
559|        # enforce a max length.
560|        if "wsgi.input_terminated" in self.environ:
561|            if self.max_content_length is not None:

563|                # read attempt is made when the client sends no data. For

568|            return stream
569|
570|        # No limit given, stream can't be read safely, return empty.
571|        if self.content_length is None:
572|            return BytesIO()
573|
574|        return _LimitedStream(stream, self.content_length)  # type: ignore[return-value]

61|def uri_to_iri(uri: str) -> str:

63|    leaving all reserved and invalid characters quoted. If the URL has
64|    a domain, it is decoded from Punycode.

66|    >>> uri_to_iri("http://xn--n3h.net/p%C3%A5th?q=%C3%A8ry%DF")
67|    'http://\\u2603.net/p\\xe5th?q=\\xe8ry%DF'
68|
69|    :param uri: The URI to convert.
70|
71|    .. versionchanged:: 3.1.9
72|        Empty username, password, and port 0 are preserved.
73|
74|    .. versionchanged:: 3.0
75|        Passing a tuple or bytes, and the ``charset`` and ``errors`` parameters,
76|        are removed.
77|
78|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3
79|        Which characters remain quoted is specific to each part of the URL.
80|
81|    .. versionchanged:: 0.15
82|        All reserved and invalid characters remain quoted. Previously,
83|        only some reserved characters were preserved, and invalid bytes
84|        were replaced instead of left quoted.
85|
86|    .. versionadded:: 0.6
87|    """
88|    parts = urlsplit(uri)
89|    path = _unquote_path(parts.path)
90|    query = _unquote_query(parts.query)
91|    fragment = _unquote_fragment(parts.fragment)
92|
93|    if parts.hostname:

97|
98|    if ":" in netloc:

100|
101|    if parts.port is not None:
102|        netloc = f"{netloc}:{parts.port}"
103|
104|    if parts.username is not None:

106|
107|        if parts.password is not None:

116|def iri_to_uri(iri: str) -> str:

120|    >>> iri_to_uri('http://\\u2603.net/p\\xe5th?q=\\xe8ry%DF')

128|    .. versionchanged:: 3.0

130|        and the ``safe_conversion`` parameter, are removed.
131|
132|    .. versionchanged:: 2.3
133|        Which characters remain unquoted is specific to each part of the URL.
134|
135|    .. versionchanged:: 0.15
136|        All reserved characters remain unquoted. Previously, only some reserved
137|        characters were left unquoted.

156|    if ":" in netloc:

159|    if parts.port is not None:
160|        netloc = f"{netloc}:{parts.port}"
161|
162|    if parts.username is not None:

165|        if parts.password is not None:

181|def _decode_idna(domain: str) -> str:
182|    try:
183|        data = domain.encode("ascii")
184|    except UnicodeEncodeError:
185|        # If the domain is not ASCII, it's decoded already.
186|        return domain
187|
188|    try:
189|        # Try decoding in one shot.
190|        return data.decode("idna")
191|    except UnicodeDecodeError:
192|        pass
193|
194|    # Decode each part separately, leaving invalid parts as punycode.
195|    parts = []
196|
197|    for part in data.split(b"."):
198|        try:
199|            parts.append(part.decode("idna"))
200|        except UnicodeDecodeError:
201|            parts.append(part.decode("ascii"))
202|
203|    return ".".join(parts)

208|    # safe = https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#percent-encoded-bytes
209|    return urlencode(items, safe="!$'()*,/:;?@")

376|        ``subdomain`` is determined to be ``abc``. If the ``server_name`` is not
377|        a suffix of the current ``Host``, such as when accessed by IP or an
378|        alternate domain name, then :attr:`default_subdomain` is used.

382|            is not given, it is determined by removing this ``host:port`` as a
383|            suffix from the ``Host`` header. If the scheme is ``http``,
384|            ``https``, ``ws``, or ``wss``, the corresponding port 80 or 443 will
385|            be removed.

443|        in the correct order after things changed.

492|    def dispatch(
493|        self,
494|        view_func: t.Callable[[str, t.Mapping[str, t.Any]], wt.WSGIApplication],
495|        path_info: str | None = None,
496|        method: str | None = None,
497|        catch_http_exceptions: bool = False,
498|    ) -> wt.WSGIApplication:
499|        """Does the complete dispatching process.  `view_func` is called with
500|        the endpoint and a dict with the values for the view.  It should
501|        look up the view function, call it, and return a response object
502|        or WSGI application.  http exceptions are not caught by default
503|        so that applications can display nicer error messages by just
504|        catching them by hand.  If you want to stick with the default
505|        error messages you can pass it ``catch_http_exceptions=True`` and
506|        it will catch the http exceptions.

508|        Here a small example for the dispatch usage::
509|
510|            from werkzeug.wrappers import Request, Response
511|            from werkzeug.wsgi import responder
512|            from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule
513|
514|            def on_index(request):
515|                return Response('Hello from the index')
516|
517|            url_map = Map([Rule('/', endpoint='index')])
518|            views = {'index': on_index}
519|
520|            @Request.application
521|            def application(request):
522|                urls = url_map.bind_to_request(request)
523|                return urls.dispatch(
524|                    lambda e, v: views[e](request, **v),
525|                    catch_http_exceptions=True
526|                )

528|        Keep in mind that this method might return exception objects, too, so
529|        use :class:`Response.force_type` to get a response object.
530|
531|        :param view_func: a function that is called with the endpoint as
532|                          first argument and the value dict as second.  Has
533|                          to dispatch to the actual view function with this
534|                          information.  (see above)
535|        :param path_info: the path info to use for matching.  Overrides the
536|                          path info specified on binding.
537|        :param method: the HTTP method used for matching.  Overrides the
538|                       method specified on binding.
539|        :param catch_http_exceptions: set to `True` to catch any of the
540|                                      werkzeug :class:`HTTPException`\\s.
541|        """
542|        try:
543|            try:
544|                endpoint, args = self.match(path_info, method)
545|            except RequestRedirect as e:
546|                return e
547|            return view_func(endpoint, args)
548|        except HTTPException as e:
549|            if catch_http_exceptions:
550|                return e
551|            raise

573|    def match(

575|        path_info: str | None = None,
576|        method: str | None = None,
577|        return_rule: bool = False,
578|        query_args: t.Mapping[str, t.Any] | str | None = None,

583|        following things can then happen:
584|
585|        - you receive a `NotFound` exception that indicates that no URL is
586|          matching.  A `NotFound` exception is also a WSGI application you
587|          can call to get a default page not found page (happens to be the
588|          same object as `werkzeug.exceptions.NotFound`)
589|
590|        - you receive a `MethodNotAllowed` exception that indicates that there
591|          is a match for this URL but not for the current request method.
592|          This is useful for RESTful applications.
593|
594|        - you receive a `RequestRedirect` exception with a `new_url`
595|          attribute.  This exception is used to notify you about a request
596|          Werkzeug requests from your WSGI application.  This is for example the
597|          case if you request ``/foo`` although the correct URL is ``/foo/``
598|          You can use the `RequestRedirect` instance as response-like object
599|          similar to all other subclasses of `HTTPException`.
600|
601|        - you receive a ``WebsocketMismatch`` exception if the only
602|          match is a WebSocket rule but the bind is an HTTP request, or
603|          if the match is an HTTP rule but the bind is a WebSocket
604|          request.

607|          a match (unless `return_rule` is True, in which case you get a tuple
608|          in the form ``(rule, arguments)``)

611|        info of the map is used (defaults to the root URL if not defined
612|        explicitly).

615|        can be used as WSGI responses. They will all render generic error or
616|        redirect pages.

618|        Here is a small example for matching:
619|
620|        >>> m = Map([
621|        ...     Rule('/', endpoint='index'),
622|        ...     Rule('/downloads/', endpoint='downloads/index'),
623|        ...     Rule('/downloads/<int:id>', endpoint='downloads/show')
624|        ... ])
625|        >>> urls = m.bind("example.com", "/")
626|        >>> urls.match("/", "GET")
627|        ('index', {})
628|        >>> urls.match("/downloads/42")
629|        ('downloads/show', {'id': 42})
630|
631|        And here is what happens on redirect and missing URLs:
632|
633|        >>> urls.match("/downloads")
634|        Traceback (most recent call last):
635|          ...
636|        RequestRedirect: http://example.com/downloads/
637|        >>> urls.match("/missing")
638|        Traceback (most recent call last):
639|          ...

662|        .. versionadded:: 0.7

665|        .. versionadded:: 0.6

111|def parse_converter_args(argstr: str) -> tuple[tuple[t.Any, ...], dict[str, t.Any]]:
112|    argstr += ","
113|    args = []
114|    kwargs = {}
115|    position = 0
116|
117|    for item in _converter_args_re.finditer(argstr):
118|        if item.start() != position:
119|            raise ValueError(
120|                f"Cannot parse converter argument '{argstr[position : item.start()]}'"
121|            )
122|
123|        value = item.group("stringval")
124|        if value is None:
125|            value = item.group("value")
126|        value = _pythonize(value)
127|        if not item.group("name"):
128|            args.append(value)
129|        else:
130|            name = item.group("name")
131|            kwargs[name] = value
132|        position = item.end()

329|class Rule(RuleFactory):
330|    """A Rule represents one URL pattern.  There are some options for `Rule`
331|    that change the way it behaves and are passed to the `Rule` constructor.
332|    Note that besides the rule-string all arguments *must* be keyword arguments
333|    in order to not break the application on Werkzeug upgrades.
334|

336|        Rule strings basically are just normal URL paths with placeholders in
337|        the format ``<converter(arguments):name>`` where the converter and the
338|        arguments are optional.  If no converter is defined the `default`
339|        converter is used which means `string` in the normal configuration.
340|

342|        If you have `strict_slashes` enabled (which is the default), all
343|        branch URLs that are matched without a trailing slash will trigger a
344|        redirect to the same URL with the missing slash appended.
345|
346|        The converters are defined on the `Map`.
347|
348|    `endpoint`
349|        The endpoint for this rule. This can be anything. A reference to a
350|        function, a string, a number etc.  The preferred way is using a string
351|        because the endpoint is used for URL generation.
352|
353|    `defaults`
354|        An optional dict with defaults for other rules with the same endpoint.
355|        This is a bit tricky but useful if you want to have unique URLs::
356|
357|            url_map = Map([
358|                Rule('/all/', defaults={'page': 1}, endpoint='all_entries'),
359|                Rule('/all/page/<int:page>', endpoint='all_entries')
360|            ])
361|
362|        If a user now visits ``http://example.com/all/page/1`` they will be
363|        redirected to ``http://example.com/all/``.  If `redirect_defaults` is
364|        disabled on the `Map` instance this will only affect the URL
365|        generation.
366|
367|    `subdomain`
368|        The subdomain rule string for this rule. If not specified the rule
369|        only matches for the `default_subdomain` of the map.  If the map is
370|        not bound to a subdomain this feature is disabled.
371|
372|        Can be useful if you want to have user profiles on different subdomains
373|        and all subdomains are forwarded to your application::
374|
375|            url_map = Map([
376|                Rule('/', subdomain='<username>', endpoint='user/homepage'),
377|                Rule('/stats', subdomain='<username>', endpoint='user/stats')
378|            ])
379|
380|    `methods`
381|        A sequence of http methods this rule applies to.  If not specified, all
382|        methods are allowed. For example this can be useful if you want different
383|        endpoints for `POST` and `GET`.  If methods are defined and the path
384|        matches but the method matched against is not in this list or in the

128|class IntegerConverter(BaseConverter):
129|    """An :class:`int` value. Available as ``int`` in rules.
130|
131|    Extraneous leading zeros are allowed. Negative zero is allowed. Therefore,
132|    there is not a 1-to-1 unique mapping between URLs and parsed values.
133|
134|    Python limits the length of strings when parsing ints. A value greater than
135|    :func:`sys.get_int_max_str_digits` will not match.
136|
137|    :param map: The map this rule is bound to.
138|    :param fixed_digits: Require a fixed number of digits. For example, ``4``
139|        will only match values like ``0001``. The negative sign is not counted,
140|        ``-0004`` is considered 4 digits.
141|    :param min: The minimum value, inclusive.
142|    :param max: The maximum value, inclusive.
143|    :param signed: Allow negative values.

146|        Non-ASCII digits are not allowed. The negative sign is not counted for
147|        ``fixed_digits``. ``to_url`` performs validation.
148|
149|    .. versionchanged:: 0.15
150|        The ``signed`` parameter was added.
151|    """
152|

154|    regex = r"[0-9]+"

156|    def __init__(
157|        self,
158|        map: Map,
159|        fixed_digits: int = 0,
160|        min: int | None = None,
161|        max: int | None = None,
162|        signed: bool = False,
163|    ) -> None:
164|        super().__init__(map)
165|        self.min = min
166|        self.max = max
167|        self.fixed_digits = fixed_digits
168|        self.signed = signed
169|
170|        if signed:
171|            self.regex = f"-?{self.regex}"

173|    def to_python(self, value: str) -> t.Any:
174|        if self.fixed_digits and len(value.removeprefix("-")) != self.fixed_digits:
175|            raise ValidationError(f"Must be {self.fixed_digits} digits.")
176|
177|        try:
178|            value_num = int(value)
179|        except ValueError as e:  # if > sys.get_int_max_str_digits()
180|            raise ValidationError() from e
181|
182|        if (self.min is not None and value_num < self.min) or (
183|            self.max is not None and value_num > self.max
184|        ):
185|            raise ValidationError("Outside of allowed range.")
186|
187|        return value_num
188|
189|    def to_url(self, value: t.Any) -> str:
190|        value = int(value)
191|
192|        if not self.signed and value < 0:
193|            raise ValidationError("Negative values are not allowed.")
194|
195|        if (self.min is not None and value < self.min) or (
196|            self.max is not None and value > self.max
197|        ):
198|            raise ValidationError("Outside of allowed range.")
199|
200|        value_str = str(value)

206|            if len(value_str) > width:

209|                )

214|class FloatConverter(BaseConverter):
215|    """A :class:`float` value. Available as ``float`` in rules.
216|
217|    Values must have an integer and decimal part, ``4.`` and ``.4`` are not
218|    allowed. Scientific notation, ``inf``, and ``nan`` are not allowed.
219|
220|    Values that are too large to fit in a float are not allowed; Python would
221|    convert them to ``inf``. Values that are too tiny are allowed; Python
222|    converts them to ``0.0``.
223|
224|    Extraneous leading and trailing zeros are allowed. Many values, such as
225|    ``0.1``, are not exactly expressible as a float and are converted to the
226|    nearest expressible value. Therefore, there is not a 1-to-1 unique mapping
227|    between URLs and parsed values.
228|
229|    :param map: The map this rule is bound to.
230|    :param min: The minimum value, inclusive.
231|    :param max: The maximum value, inclusive.
232|    :param signed: Allow negative values.
233|
234|    .. versionchanged:: 3.2
235|        Non-ASCII digits are not allowed. Values that are too large and overflow
236|        to ``inf`` are not allowed. ``to_url`` performs validation and does not
237|        produce scientific notation.
238|
239|    .. versionchanged:: 0.15
240|        The ``signed`` parameter was added.
241|    """
242|
243|    weight = 50
244|    regex = r"[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"
245|
246|    def __init__(
247|        self,
248|        map: Map,
249|        min: float | None = None,
250|        max: float | None = None,
251|        signed: bool = False,
252|    ) -> None:
253|        super().__init__(map)
254|        self.min = min
255|        self.max = max
256|        self.signed = signed
257|
258|        if signed:
259|            self.regex = f"-?{self.regex}"
260|
261|    def to_python(self, value: str) -> t.Any:
262|        value_num: float = float(value)
263|        # will convert too tiny to 0.0, too large to inf
264|
265|        if math.isinf(value_num):
266|            raise ValidationError("Too large.")
267|
268|        if (self.min is not None and value_num < self.min) or (
269|            self.max is not None and value_num > self.max
270|        ):
271|            raise ValidationError("Outside of allowed range.")
272|
273|        return value_num
274|
275|    def to_url(self, value: t.Any) -> str:
276|        value = float(value)
277|
278|        if not math.isfinite(value):
279|            raise ValidationError("Infinity or NaN are not allowed.")
280|
281|        if not self.signed and value < 0:
282|            raise ValidationError("Negative values are not allowed.")
283|
284|        if (self.min is not None and value < self.min) or (
285|            self.max is not None and value > self.max
286|        ):
287|            raise ValidationError("Outside of allowed range.")
288|
289|        # Use `str(value)` if it doesn't produce scientific notation.
290|        if "e" not in (value_str := str(value)):
291|            return value_str
292|
293|        sig, _, exp_str = value_str.partition("e")
294|        left, _, right = sig.partition(".")
295|        exp = int(exp_str)
296|
297|        # A big number. Expand trailing zeros in the integer part.
298|        if exp > 0:
299|            return f"{left}{right}{'0' * (exp - len(right))}.0"
300|
301|        # A small number. Expand leading zeros in the fraction part.
302|        if left.startswith("-"):
303|            left = left[1:]
304|            start = "-0"
305|        else:
306|            start = "0"
307|
308|        return f"{start}.{'0' * (-exp - len(left))}{left}{right}"

51|def stream_encode_multipart(
52|    data: t.Mapping[str, t.Any],
53|    use_tempfile: bool = True,
54|    threshold: int = 1024 * 500,
55|    boundary: str | None = None,
56|) -> tuple[t.IO[bytes], int, str]:
57|    """Encode a dict of values (either strings or file descriptors or
58|    :class:`FileStorage` objects.) into a multipart encoded string stored
59|    in a file descriptor.
60|
61|    This is not secure and must only be used during testing, never in applications.
62|
63|    .. versionchanged:: 3.0
64|        The ``charset`` parameter was removed.
65|    """
66|    if boundary is None:
67|        boundary = f"---------------WerkzeugFormPart_{time()}{random()}"
68|
69|    stream: t.IO[bytes] = BytesIO()
70|    total_length = 0
71|    on_disk = False
72|    write_binary: t.Callable[[bytes], int]
73|
74|    if use_tempfile:
75|
76|        def write_binary(s: bytes) -> int:
77|            nonlocal stream, total_length, on_disk
78|
79|            if on_disk:
80|                return stream.write(s)
81|            else:
82|                length = len(s)
83|
84|                if length + total_length <= threshold:
85|                    stream.write(s)
86|                else:
87|                    new_stream = t.cast(t.IO[bytes], TemporaryFile("wb+"))
88|                    new_stream.write(stream.getvalue())  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
89|                    new_stream.write(s)
90|                    stream = new_stream
91|                    on_disk = True
92|
93|                total_length += length
94|                return length
95|
96|    else:
97|        write_binary = stream.write
98|
99|    encoder = MultipartEncoder(boundary.encode())
100|    write_binary(encoder.send_event(Preamble(data=b"")))
101|    for key, value in _iter_data(data):
102|        reader = getattr(value, "read", None)
103|        if reader is not None:
104|            filename = getattr(value, "filename", getattr(value, "name", None))
105|            content_type = getattr(value, "content_type", None)
106|            if content_type is None:
107|                content_type = (
108|                    filename
109|                    and mimetypes.guess_type(filename)[0]
110|                    or "application/octet-stream"
111|                )
112|            headers = value.headers
113|            headers.update([("Content-Type", content_type)])
114|            if filename is None:
115|                write_binary(encoder.send_event(Field(name=key, headers=headers)))
116|            else:
117|                write_binary(
118|                    encoder.send_event(
119|                        File(name=key, filename=filename, headers=headers)
120|                    )
121|                )
122|            while True:
123|                chunk = reader(16384)
124|
125|                if not chunk:
126|                    write_binary(encoder.send_event(Data(data=chunk, more_data=False)))
127|                    break
128|
129|                write_binary(encoder.send_event(Data(data=chunk, more_data=True)))
130|        else:
131|            if not isinstance(value, str):
132|                value = str(value)
133|            write_binary(encoder.send_event(Field(name=key, headers=Headers())))
134|            write_binary(encoder.send_event(Data(data=value.encode(), more_data=False)))
135|
136|    write_binary(encoder.send_event(Epilogue(data=b"")))
137|
138|    length = stream.tell()
139|    stream.seek(0)
140|    return stream, length, boundary

143|def encode_multipart(
144|    values: t.Mapping[str, t.Any], boundary: str | None = None
145|) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
146|    """Like `stream_encode_multipart` but returns a tuple in the form
147|    (``boundary``, ``data``) where data is bytes.
148|
149|    This is not secure and must only be used during testing, never in applications.
150|
151|    .. versionchanged:: 3.0

154|    stream, length, boundary = stream_encode_multipart(

160|def _iter_data(data: t.Mapping[str, t.Any]) -> t.Iterator[tuple[str, t.Any]]:
161|    """Iterate over a mapping that might have a list of values, yielding
162|    all key, value pairs. Almost like iter_multi_items but only allows
163|    lists, not tuples, of values so tuples can be used for files.
164|    """
165|    if isinstance(data, MultiDict):
166|        yield from data.items(multi=True)
167|    else:
168|        for key, value in data.items():
169|            if isinstance(value, list):
170|                for v in value:
171|                    yield key, v
172|            else:
173|                yield key, value

1231|def run_wsgi_app(
1232|    app: wt.WSGIApplication, environ: wt.WSGIEnvironment, buffered: bool = False
1233|) -> tuple[t.Iterable[bytes], str, Headers]:
1234|    """Return a tuple in the form (app_iter, status, headers) of the
1235|    application output.  This works best if you pass it an application that
1236|    returns an iterator all the time.
1237|
1238|    Sometimes applications may use the `write()` callable returned
1239|    by the `start_response` function.  This tries to resolve such edge
1240|    cases automatically.  But if you don't get the expected output you
1241|    should set `buffered` to `True` which enforces buffering.
1242|
1243|    If passed an invalid WSGI application the behavior of this function is
1244|    undefined.  Never pass non-conforming WSGI applications to this function.
1245|
1246|    :param app: the application to execute.
1247|    :param buffered: set to `True` to enforce buffering.
1248|    :return: tuple in the form ``(app_iter, status, headers)``
1249|    """
1250|    # Copy environ to ensure any mutations by the app (ProxyFix, for
1251|    # example) don't affect subsequent requests (such as redirects).
1252|    environ = _get_environ(environ).copy()
1253|    status: str
1254|    response: tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] | None = None
1255|    buffer: list[bytes] = []
1256|
1257|    def start_response(
1258|        status: str,
1259|        headers: list[tuple[str, str]],
1260|        exc_info: tuple[type[BaseException], BaseException, TracebackType]
1261|        | tuple[None, None, None]
1262|        | None = None,
1263|    ) -> t.Callable[[bytes], object]:
1264|        nonlocal response
1265|
1266|        if exc_info:
1267|            try:
1268|                raise exc_info[1].with_traceback(exc_info[2])  # type: ignore[union-attr]
1269|            finally:
1270|                exc_info = None
1271|
1272|        response = (status, headers)
1273|        return buffer.append
1274|
1275|    app_rv = app(environ, start_response)
1276|    close_func = getattr(app_rv, "close", None)
1277|    app_iter: t.Iterable[bytes] = iter(app_rv)
1278|
1279|    # when buffering we emit the close call early and convert the
1280|    # application iterator into a regular list
1281|    if buffered:
1282|        try:
1283|            app_iter = list(app_iter)
1284|        finally:
1285|            if close_func is not None:
1286|                close_func()
1287|
1288|    # Otherwise, iterate until a response, chain any received data with the
1289|    # original, and restore a close callable if needed.
1290|    else:
1291|        for item in app_iter:
1292|            buffer.append(item)
1293|
1294|            if response is not None:
1295|                break
1296|
1297|        if buffer:
1298|            app_iter = chain(buffer, app_iter)
1299|
1300|        if close_func is not None and app_iter is not app_rv:
1301|            app_iter = ClosingIterator(app_iter, close_func)
1302|
1303|    status, headers = response  # type: ignore[misc]
1304|    return app_iter, status, Headers(headers)
