126|def _process_traceback(
127|    exc: BaseException,
128|    te: traceback.TracebackException | None = None,
129|    *,
130|    skip: int = 0,
131|    hide: bool = True,
132|) -> traceback.TracebackException:
133|    if te is None:
134|        te = traceback.TracebackException.from_exception(exc, lookup_lines=False)
135|
136|    # Get the frames the same way StackSummary.extract did, in order
137|    # to match each frame with the FrameSummary to augment.
138|    frame_gen = traceback.walk_tb(exc.__traceback__)
139|    limit = getattr(sys, "tracebacklimit", None)
140|
141|    if limit is not None:
142|        if limit < 0:
143|            limit = 0
144|
145|        frame_gen = itertools.islice(frame_gen, limit)
146|
147|    if skip:
148|        frame_gen = itertools.islice(frame_gen, skip, None)
149|        del te.stack[:skip]
150|
151|    new_stack: list[DebugFrameSummary] = []
152|    hidden = False
153|
154|    # Match each frame with the FrameSummary that was generated.
155|    # Hide frames using Paste's __traceback_hide__ rules. Replace
156|    # all visible FrameSummary with DebugFrameSummary.
157|    for (f, _), fs in zip(frame_gen, te.stack, strict=True):
158|        if hide:
159|            hide_value = f.f_locals.get("__traceback_hide__", False)
160|
161|            if hide_value in {"before", "before_and_this"}:
162|                new_stack = []
163|                hidden = False
164|
165|                if hide_value == "before_and_this":
166|                    continue
167|            elif hide_value in {"reset", "reset_and_this"}:
168|                hidden = False
169|
170|                if hide_value == "reset_and_this":
171|                    continue
172|            elif hide_value in {"after", "after_and_this"}:
173|                hidden = True
174|
175|                if hide_value == "after_and_this":
176|                    continue
177|            elif hide_value or hidden:
178|                continue
179|
180|        frame_args: dict[str, t.Any] = {
181|            "filename": fs.filename,
182|            "lineno": fs.lineno,
183|            "colno": fs.colno,
184|            "end_colno": fs.end_colno,
185|            "name": fs.name,
186|            "locals": f.f_locals,
187|            "globals": f.f_globals,
188|        }
189|        new_stack.append(DebugFrameSummary(**frame_args))
190|
191|    # The codeop module is used to compile code from the interactive
192|    # debugger. Hide any codeop frames from the bottom of the traceback.
193|    while new_stack:
194|        module = new_stack[0].global_ns.get("__name__")
195|
196|        if module is None:
197|            module = new_stack[0].local_ns.get("__name__")
198|
199|        if module == "codeop":
200|            del new_stack[0]
201|        else:
202|            break

204|    te.stack[:] = new_stack

206|    if te.__context__:
207|        context_exc = t.cast(BaseException, exc.__context__)
208|        te.__context__ = _process_traceback(context_exc, te.__context__, hide=hide)
209|
210|    if te.__cause__:
211|        cause_exc = t.cast(BaseException, exc.__cause__)
212|        te.__cause__ = _process_traceback(cause_exc, te.__cause__, hide=hide)
213|
214|    return te

63|# Multipart line breaks MUST be CRLF (\r\n) by RFC-7578, except that
64|# many implementations break this and either use CR or LF alone.

67|LINE_BREAK_RE = re.compile(LINE_BREAK, re.MULTILINE)

77|class MultipartDecoder:
78|    """Decodes a multipart message as bytes into Python events.
79|
80|    The part data is returned as available to allow the caller to save
81|    the data from memory to disk, if desired.
82|
83|    .. versionchanged:: 3.1.4
84|        Handle chunks that split a``\r\n`` sequence.
85|    """
86|
87|    def __init__(
88|        self,
89|        boundary: bytes,
90|        max_form_memory_size: int | None = None,
91|        *,
92|        max_parts: int | None = None,
93|    ) -> None:
94|        self.buffer = bytearray()
95|        self.complete = False
96|        self.max_form_memory_size = max_form_memory_size
97|        self.max_parts = max_parts
98|        self.state = State.PREAMBLE
99|        self.boundary = boundary
100|
101|        # Note in the below \h i.e. horizontal whitespace is used
102|        # as [^\S\n\r] as \h isn't supported in python.
103|
104|        # The preamble must end with a boundary where the boundary is
105|        # prefixed by a line break, RFC2046. Except that many
106|        # implementations including Werkzeug's tests omit the line
107|        # break prefix. In addition the first boundary could be the
108|        # epilogue boundary (for empty form-data) hence the matching
109|        # group to understand if it is an epilogue boundary.
110|        self.preamble_re = re.compile(
111|            rb"%s?--%s(--[^\S\n\r]*%s?|[^\S\n\r]*%s)"
112|            % (LINE_BREAK, re.escape(boundary), LINE_BREAK, LINE_BREAK),
113|            re.MULTILINE,
114|        )
115|        # A boundary must include a line break prefix and suffix, and
116|        # may include trailing whitespace. In addition the boundary
117|        # could be the epilogue boundary hence the matching group to
118|        # understand if it is an epilogue boundary.
119|        self.boundary_re = re.compile(
120|            rb"%s--%s(--[^\S\n\r]*%s?|[^\S\n\r]*%s)"
121|            % (LINE_BREAK, re.escape(boundary), LINE_BREAK, LINE_BREAK),
122|            re.MULTILINE,
123|        )
124|        self._search_position = 0
125|        self._parts_decoded = 0

127|    def receive_data(self, data: bytes | None) -> None:

130|        elif (

132|            and len(self.buffer) + len(data) > self.max_form_memory_size
133|        ):

135|            # Also checked across accumulated events in MultiPartParser.
136|            raise RequestEntityTooLarge()

138|            self.buffer.extend(data)

225|    def _parse_headers(self, data: bytes | bytearray) -> Headers:

238|    def _parse_data(
239|        self, data: bytes | bytearray, *, start: bool
240|    ) -> tuple[bytes, int, bool]:

242|        if start:

262|                data_end = match.start()
263|                del_index = match.end()
264|            else:

268|            more_data = match is None

271|    def _last_partial_boundary_index(self, data: bytes | bytearray) -> int:

274|        # position of a LF or a CR, unless that position is more
275|        # than a complete boundary from the end in which case there
276|        # is no partial boundary.
277|        complete_boundary_index = len(data) - len(b"\r\n--" + self.boundary)
278|        try:
279|            last_nl = data.rindex(b"\n")
280|        except ValueError:
281|            last_nl = len(data)
282|        else:
283|            if last_nl < complete_boundary_index:
284|                last_nl = len(data)
285|        try:
286|            last_cr = data.rindex(b"\r")
287|        except ValueError:
288|            last_cr = len(data)
289|        else:
290|            if last_cr < complete_boundary_index:
291|                last_cr = len(data)
292|        return min(last_nl, last_cr)

295|class MultipartEncoder:
296|    """Used by the test client to create a multipart body. This is not secure
297|    and must only be used during testing, never in applications.
298|
299|    :meta private:
300|    """
301|
302|    def __init__(self, boundary: bytes) -> None:
303|        self.boundary = boundary
304|        self.state = State.PREAMBLE
305|
306|    def send_event(self, event: Event) -> bytes:
307|        if isinstance(event, Preamble) and self.state == State.PREAMBLE:
308|            self.state = State.PART
309|            return event.data
310|        elif isinstance(event, (Field, File)) and self.state in {
311|            State.PREAMBLE,
312|            State.PART,
313|            State.DATA,
314|        }:
315|            data = b"\r\n--" + self.boundary + b"\r\n"
316|            data += b'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="%s"' % event.name.encode()
317|            if isinstance(event, File):
318|                data += b'; filename="%s"' % event.filename.encode()
319|            data += b"\r\n"
320|            for name, value in t.cast(Field, event).headers:
321|                if name.lower() != "content-disposition":
322|                    data += f"{name}: {value}\r\n".encode()
323|            self.state = State.DATA_START
324|            return data
325|        elif isinstance(event, Data) and self.state == State.DATA_START:
326|            self.state = State.DATA
327|            if len(event.data) > 0:
328|                return b"\r\n" + event.data
329|            else:
330|                return event.data
331|        elif isinstance(event, Data) and self.state == State.DATA:
332|            return event.data
333|        elif isinstance(event, Epilogue):
334|            self.state = State.COMPLETE
335|            return b"\r\n--" + self.boundary + b"--\r\n" + event.data
336|        else:
337|            raise ValueError(f"Cannot generate {event} in state: {self.state}")

25|def host_is_trusted(
26|    hostname: str | None, trusted_list: t.Collection[str] | None = None
27|) -> bool:
28|    """Perform some checks on a ``Host`` header ``host:port``. The host must be
29|    made up of valid characters, but this does not check validity beyond that.
30|    If a list of trusted domains is given, the domain must match one.
31|
32|    :param hostname: The ``Host`` header ``host:port`` to check.
33|    :param trusted_list: A list of trusted domains to match. These should
34|        already be IDNA encoded, but will be encoded if needed. If a name starts
35|        with a dot it will match as a suffix, accepting all subdomains. If empty
36|        or ``None``, all domains are allowed.
37|
38|    .. deprecated:: 3.2
39|        Will be private in Werkzeug 4.0. Use ``Request.trusted_hosts`` and
40|        ``Request.host`` instead.
41|
42|    .. versionchanged:: 3.2
43|        The value's characters are validated.
44|
45|    .. versionchanged:: 3.2
46|        ``trusted_list`` defaults to ``None``.
47|
48|    .. versionadded:: 0.9
49|    """
50|    if not hostname:
51|        return False
52|
53|    if (m := _host_re.fullmatch(hostname)) is None:
54|        return False
55|
56|    hostname, port_str = m.groups()
57|
58|    if port_str and not (1 <= int(port_str) <= 65535):
59|        return False
60|
61|    if not trusted_list:
62|        return True
63|
64|    if isinstance(trusted_list, str):
65|        trusted_list = [trusted_list]
66|
67|    for ref in trusted_list:
68|        if ref.startswith("."):
69|            ref = ref[1:]
70|            suffix_match = True
71|        else:
72|            suffix_match = False
73|
74|        try:
75|            ref = ref.encode("idna").decode("ascii")
76|        except UnicodeEncodeError:
77|            return False
78|
79|        if ref == hostname or (suffix_match and hostname.endswith(f".{ref}")):
80|            return True
81|
82|    return False

85|def get_host(
86|    scheme: str,
87|    host_header: str | None,
88|    server: tuple[str, int | None] | None = None,
89|    trusted_hosts: t.Collection[str] | None = None,
90|) -> str:
91|    """Get and validate a request's ``host:port`` based on the given values.
92|
93|    The ``Host`` header sent by the client is preferred. Otherwise, the server's
94|    configured address is used. The port is omitted if it matches the standard
95|    HTTP or HTTPS ports.
96|
97|    The value is passed through :func:`host_is_trusted`. The host must be made
98|    up of valid characters, but this does not check validity beyond that. If a
99|    list of trusted domains is given, the domain must match one.
100|
101|    If the host header is not available, such as for HTTP/0.9 and 1.0, or it has
102|    invalid characters, the empty string is returned. Subdomain and host
103|    routing, and external URL building, will not work in these cases.
104|
105|    :param scheme: The protocol of the request. Used to omit the standard ports
106|        80 and 443.
107|    :param host_header: The ``Host`` header value.
108|    :param server: The server's configured address ``(host, port)``. The server
109|        may be using a Unix socket and give ``(path, None)``; this is ignored as
110|        it would not produce a useful host value.
111|    :param trusted_hosts: A list of trusted domains to match. These should
112|        already be IDNA encoded, but will be encoded if needed. The port is
113|        ignored for this check. If a name starts with a dot it will match as a
114|        suffix, accepting all subdomains. If empty or ``None``, all domains are
115|        allowed.
116|
117|    :return: Host, with port if necessary.
118|    :raise .SecurityError: If the host is not trusted.
119|
120|    .. versionchanged:: 3.2
121|        When using the server address, Unix sockets are ignored.
122|
123|    .. versionchanged:: 3.1.8
124|        The empty string is again returned if no host header value is available,
125|        or if the characters are invalid.
126|
127|    .. versionchanged:: 3.1.7
128|        The characters of the host value are validated. The empty string is no
129|        longer allowed if no header value is available.
130|
131|    .. versionchanged:: 3.1.3
132|        If ``SERVER_NAME`` is IPv6, it is wrapped in ``[]``.
133|    """
134|    if host_header is not None:
135|        host = host_header
136|    # The port server[1] will be None for a Unix socket. Ignore in that case.
137|    elif server is not None and server[1] is not None:
138|        host = server[0]
139|
140|        # If SERVER_NAME is IPv6, wrap it in [] to match Host header.
141|        # Check for : because domain or IPv4 can't have that.
142|        if ":" in host and host[0] != "[":
143|            host = f"[{host}]"
144|
145|        host = f"{host}:{server[1]}"
146|    else:
147|        # Pass through empty host from HTTP/0.9 and 1.0.
148|        return ""
149|
150|    if scheme in {"http", "ws"}:
151|        host = host.removesuffix(":80")
152|    elif scheme in {"https", "wss"}:
153|        host = host.removesuffix(":443")
154|
155|    if not host_is_trusted(host, trusted_hosts):
156|        if trusted_hosts:
157|            raise SecurityError(f"Host {host!r} is not trusted.")
158|
159|        # Invalid characters, treat as empty.
160|        return ""
161|
162|    return host

165|def get_current_url(
166|    scheme: str,
167|    host: str,
168|    root_path: str | None = None,
169|    path: str | None = None,
170|    query_string: bytes | None = None,
171|) -> str:
172|    """Recreate the URL for a request. If an optional part isn't
173|    provided, it and subsequent parts are not included in the URL.
174|
175|    The URL is an IRI, not a URI, so it may contain Unicode characters.
176|    Use :func:`~werkzeug.urls.iri_to_uri` to convert it to ASCII.
177|
178|    :param scheme: The protocol the request used, like ``"https"``.
179|    :param host: The host the request was made to. See :func:`get_host`.
180|    :param root_path: Prefix that the application is mounted under. This
181|        is prepended to ``path``.
182|    :param path: The path part of the URL after ``root_path``.
183|    :param query_string: The portion of the URL after the "?".
184|    """
185|    url = [scheme, "://", host]
186|
187|    if root_path is None:
188|        url.append("/")
189|        return uri_to_iri("".join(url))
190|
191|    # safe = https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-path-segment-string
192|    # as well as percent for things that are already quoted
193|    url.append(quote(root_path.rstrip("/"), safe="!$&'()*+,/:;=@%"))
194|    url.append("/")
195|
196|    if path is None:
197|        return uri_to_iri("".join(url))
198|
199|    url.append(quote(path.lstrip("/"), safe="!$&'()*+,/:;=@%"))
200|
201|    if query_string:

48|        return (

51|            ).hex(),

89|    -   ``pbkdf2``, less secure. The parameters are ``hash_method`` and ``iterations``,
90|        the default is ``pbkdf2:sha256:600000``. See :func:`hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac`.

93|    deprecated and removed if they are no longer considered secure. To migrate old
94|    hashes, you may generate a new hash when checking an old hash, or you may contact
95|    users with a link to reset their password.

143|def safe_join(directory: str, *untrusted: str) -> str | None:
144|    """Safely join zero or more untrusted path components to a trusted base
145|    directory to avoid escaping the base directory. Return ``None`` if the path
146|    is not safe.
147|
148|    The untrusted path is assumed to be from/for a URL, such as for serving
149|    files. Therefore, it should only use the forward slash ``/`` path separator,
150|    and will be joined using that separator. On Windows, the backslash ``\\``
151|    separator is not allowed.
152|
153|    This only considers the path name, it does not validate if it does or does
154|    not exist, if it is a symlink, or other properties of the file or
155|    filesystem. It's up to the application to ensure that the contents of
156|    ``directory`` can be trusted.
157|
158|    On Windows, special device names such as ``CON`` and ``NUL`` are not
159|    allowed, as this is used for serving files with :func:`.send_from_directory`
160|    and those files will hang when read.
161|
162|    NTFS alternate data streams (ADS) like ``filename:stream`` are
163|    allowed. :func:`.secure_filename` will remove the ``:`` when saving.
164|
165|    :param directory: The trusted base directory.
166|    :param untrusted: The untrusted path components relative to the
167|        base directory.
168|    :return: A safe path, otherwise ``None``.
169|
170|    .. versionchanged:: 3.1.9
171|        Special device names with empty ADS stream markers are not allowed on
172|        Windows.
173|
174|    .. versionchanged:: 3.1.6
175|        Special device names in multi-segment paths are not allowed on Windows.
176|
177|    .. versionchanged:: 3.1.5
178|        More special device names, regardless of extension or trailing spaces,
179|        are not allowed on Windows.
180|
181|    .. versionchanged:: 3.1.4
182|        Special device names are not allowed on Windows.
183|    """
184|    if not directory:
185|        # Ensure we end up with ./path if directory="" is given,
186|        # otherwise the first untrusted part could become trusted.
187|        directory = "."
188|
189|    parts = [directory]
190|
191|    for part in untrusted:
192|        if not part:
193|            continue
194|
195|        part = posixpath.normpath(part)
196|
197|        if (
198|            os.path.isabs(part)
199|            # ntpath.isabs doesn't catch this
200|            or part.startswith("/")
201|            or part == ".."
202|            or part.startswith("../")
203|            or any(sep in part for sep in _os_alt_seps)

205|                os.name == "nt"
206|                and any(
207|                    p.partition(":")[0].partition(".")[0].strip().upper()
208|                    in _windows_device_files
209|                    for p in part.split("/")
210|                )
211|            )
212|        ):
213|            return None
214|
215|        parts.append(part)
216|
217|    return posixpath.join(*parts)

91|    used by the dev server, which must not be used in production. A production
92|    WSGI server will have its own robust, secure chunk handler.

96|        self._rfile = rfile

101|        return True

103|    def read_chunk_len(self) -> int:
104|        try:
105|            line = self._rfile.readline(100).decode("latin1").removesuffix("\r\n")

107|        except ValueError as e:
108|            raise OSError("Invalid chunk header") from e
109|        if _len < 0:
110|            raise OSError("Negative chunk length not allowed")
111|        return _len

113|    def readinto(self, buf: bytearray) -> int:  # type: ignore[override]
114|        read = 0

116|            if self._len == 0:
117|                # This is the first chunk or we fully consumed the previous
118|                # one. Read the next length of the next chunk
119|                self._len = self.read_chunk_len()
120|
121|            if self._len == 0:
122|                # Found the final chunk of size 0. The stream is now exhausted,
123|                # but there is still a final newline that should be consumed
124|                self._done = True
125|
126|            if self._len > 0:
127|                # There is data (left) in this chunk, so append it to the
128|                # buffer. If this operation fully consumes the chunk, this will
129|                # reset self._len to 0.
130|                n = min(len(buf), self._len)
131|
132|                # If (read + chunk size) becomes more than len(buf), buf will
133|                # grow beyond the original size and read more data than
134|                # required. So only read as much data as can fit in buf.
135|                if read + n > len(buf):
136|                    buf[read:] = self._rfile.read(len(buf) - read)
137|                    self._len -= len(buf) - read
138|                    read = len(buf)

141|                    self._len -= n

144|            if self._len == 0:

146|                # consumed. This also applies to the 0-sized final chunk
147|                terminator = self._rfile.readline(2)
148|                if terminator not in (b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\r"):
149|                    raise OSError("Missing chunk terminating newline")

221|            environ["wsgi.input"] = DechunkedInput(environ["wsgi.input"])
222|
223|        # Per RFC 2616, if the URL is absolute, use that as the host.
224|        # We're using "has a scheme" to indicate an absolute URL.
225|        if request_url.scheme and request_url.netloc:
226|            environ["HTTP_HOST"] = request_url.netloc
227|
228|        try:
229|            # binary_form=False gives nicer information, but wouldn't be compatible with
230|            # what Nginx or Apache could return.
231|            peer_cert = self.connection.getpeercert(binary_form=True)
232|            if peer_cert is not None:
233|                # Nginx and Apache use PEM format.
234|                environ["SSL_CLIENT_CERT"] = ssl.DER_cert_to_PEM_cert(peer_cert)
235|        except ValueError:
236|            # SSL handshake hasn't finished.
237|            self.server.log("error", "Cannot fetch SSL peer certificate info")
238|        except AttributeError:
239|            # Not using TLS, the socket will not have getpeercert().
240|            pass
241|
242|        return environ
243|
244|    def run_wsgi(self) -> None:
245|        self.environ = environ = self.make_environ()
246|        status_set: str | None = None
247|        headers_set: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None
248|        status_sent: str | None = None
249|        headers_sent: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None
250|        chunk_response: bool = False
251|
252|        def write(data: bytes) -> None:
253|            nonlocal status_sent, headers_sent, chunk_response
254|            assert status_set is not None, "write() before start_response"
255|            assert headers_set is not None, "write() before start_response"
256|            if status_sent is None:
257|                status_sent = status_set
258|                headers_sent = headers_set
259|                try:
260|                    code_str, msg = status_sent.split(None, 1)
261|                except ValueError:
262|                    code_str, msg = status_sent, ""
263|                code = int(code_str)
264|                self.send_response(code, msg)
265|                header_keys = set()
266|                for key, value in headers_sent:
267|                    self.send_header(key, value)
268|                    header_keys.add(key.lower())
269|
270|                # Use chunked transfer encoding if there is no content
271|                # length. Do not use for 1xx and 204 responses. 304
272|                # responses and HEAD requests are also excluded, which
273|                # is the more conservative behavior and matches other
274|                # parts of the code.
275|                # https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7230.html#rfc.section.3.3.1
276|                if (
277|                    not (
278|                        "content-length" in header_keys
279|                        or environ["REQUEST_METHOD"] == "HEAD"
280|                        or (100 <= code < 200)
281|                        or code in {204, 304}
282|                    )
283|                    and self.protocol_version >= "HTTP/1.1"
284|                ):
285|                    chunk_response = True
286|                    self.send_header("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")
287|
288|                # Always close the connection. This disables HTTP/1.1
289|                # keep-alive connections. They aren't handled well by
290|                # Python's http.server because it doesn't know how to
291|                # drain the stream before the next request line.
292|                self.send_header("Connection", "close")
293|                self.end_headers()
294|
295|            assert isinstance(data, bytes), "applications must write bytes"
296|
297|            if data:
298|                if chunk_response:
299|                    self.wfile.write(hex(len(data))[2:].encode())
300|                    self.wfile.write(b"\r\n")
301|
302|                self.wfile.write(data)
303|
304|                if chunk_response:
305|                    self.wfile.write(b"\r\n")
306|
307|            self.wfile.flush()
308|
309|        def start_response(
310|            status: str,
311|            headers: list[tuple[str, str]],
312|            exc_info: tuple[type[BaseException], BaseException, TracebackType]
313|            | tuple[None, None, None]
314|            | None = None,
315|        ) -> t.Callable[[bytes], object]:
316|            nonlocal status_set, headers_set
317|            if exc_info:
318|                try:
319|                    if headers_sent:
320|                        raise exc_info[1].with_traceback(exc_info[2])  # type: ignore[union-attr]
321|                finally:
322|                    exc_info = None
323|            elif headers_set:
324|                raise AssertionError("Headers already set")
325|            status_set = status
326|            headers_set = headers
327|            return write
328|
329|        def execute(app: wt.WSGIApplication) -> None:
330|            application_iter = app(environ, start_response)
331|            try:
332|                for data in application_iter:
333|                    write(data)
334|                if not headers_sent:
335|                    write(b"")
336|                if chunk_response:
337|                    self.wfile.write(b"0\r\n\r\n")
338|            finally:
339|                if hasattr(application_iter, "close"):
340|                    close_iter: contextlib.AbstractContextManager[t.Any] = (
341|                        contextlib.closing(application_iter)
342|                    )
343|                else:
344|                    close_iter = contextlib.nullcontext()
345|
346|                with close_iter, selectors.DefaultSelector() as selector:
347|                    # Check for any remaining data in the read socket, and discard it.
348|                    # This will read past request.max_content_length, but lets the
349|                    # client see a 413 response instead of a connection reset failure.
350|                    # If we supported keep-alive connections, this naive approach would
351|                    # break by reading the next request line. Since we know that write
352|                    # (above) closes every connection we can read everything.
353|                    selector.register(self.connection, selectors.EVENT_READ)
354|                    total_size = 0
355|                    total_reads = 0
356|
357|                    # A timeout of 0 tends to fail because a client needs a small amount
358|                    # of time to continue sending its data.
359|                    while selector.select(timeout=0.01):
360|                        # Only read 10MB into memory at a time.
361|                        data = self.rfile.read(10_000_000)
362|                        total_size += len(data)
363|                        total_reads += 1
364|
365|                        # Stop reading on no data, >=10GB, or 1000 reads. If a client
366|                        # sends more than that, they'll get a connection reset failure.
367|                        if (
368|                            not data
369|                            or total_size >= 10_000_000_000
370|                            or total_reads > 1_000
371|                        ):
372|                            break
373|
374|        try:
375|            execute(self.server.app)
376|        except connection_dropped_errors as e:
377|            self.connection_dropped(e, environ)
378|        except Exception as e:
379|            if self.server.passthrough_errors:
380|                raise
381|
382|            if status_sent is not None and chunk_response:
383|                self.close_connection = True
384|
385|            try:
386|                # if we haven't yet sent the headers but they are set
387|                # we roll back to be able to set them again.
388|                if status_sent is None:
389|                    status_set = None
390|                    headers_set = None
391|                execute(InternalServerError())
392|            except Exception:
393|                pass
394|
395|            from .debug.tbtools import DebugTraceback
396|
397|            msg = DebugTraceback(e).render_traceback_text()
398|            self.server.log("error", f"Error on request:\n{msg}")
399|
400|    def handle(self) -> None:
401|        """Handles a request ignoring dropped connections."""
402|        try:
403|            super().handle()
404|        except (ConnectionError, TimeoutError) as e:
405|            self.connection_dropped(e)
406|        except Exception as e:
407|            if self.server.ssl_context is not None and is_ssl_error(e):
408|                self.log_error("SSL error occurred: %s", e)
409|            else:
410|                raise

445|    def log_request(self, code: int | str = "-", size: int | str = "-") -> None:
446|        try:
447|            path = uri_to_iri(self.path)
448|            msg = f"{self.command} {path} {self.request_version}"
449|        except AttributeError:
450|            # path isn't set if the requestline was bad
451|            msg = self.requestline

454|        msg = msg.translate(self._control_char_table)
455|        code = str(code)

457|        if code.startswith("1"):  # 1xx - Informational
458|            msg = _ansi_style(msg, "bold")
459|        elif code == "200":  # 2xx - Success
460|            pass
461|        elif code == "304":  # 304 - Resource Not Modified
462|            msg = _ansi_style(msg, "cyan")
463|        elif code.startswith("3"):  # 3xx - Redirection
464|            msg = _ansi_style(msg, "green")
465|        elif code == "404":  # 404 - Resource Not Found
466|            msg = _ansi_style(msg, "yellow")
467|        elif code.startswith("4"):  # 4xx - Client Error
468|            msg = _ansi_style(msg, "bold", "red")
469|        else:  # 5xx, or any other response
470|            msg = _ansi_style(msg, "bold", "magenta")
471|
472|        self.log("info", '"%s" %s %s', msg, code, size)

490|def _ansi_style(value: str, *styles: str) -> str:
491|    codes = {
492|        "bold": 1,
493|        "red": 31,
494|        "green": 32,
495|        "yellow": 33,
496|        "magenta": 35,
497|        "cyan": 36,
498|    }
499|
500|    for style in styles:
501|        value = f"\x1b[{codes[style]}m{value}"

506|def generate_adhoc_ssl_pair(
507|    cn: str | None = None,
508|) -> tuple[Certificate, RSAPrivateKeyWithSerialization]:
509|    try:
510|        from cryptography import x509
511|        from cryptography.hazmat.backends import default_backend
512|        from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
513|        from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
514|        from cryptography.x509.oid import NameOID
515|    except ImportError:
516|        raise TypeError(
517|            "Using ad-hoc certificates requires the cryptography library."
518|        ) from None
519|
520|    backend = default_backend()
521|    pkey = rsa.generate_private_key(
522|        public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048, backend=backend
523|    )
524|
525|    # pretty damn sure that this is not actually accepted by anyone
526|    if cn is None:
527|        cn = "*"
528|
529|    subject = x509.Name(
530|        [
531|            x509.NameAttribute(NameOID.ORGANIZATION_NAME, "Dummy Certificate"),
532|            x509.NameAttribute(NameOID.COMMON_NAME, cn),
533|        ]
534|    )
535|
536|    backend = default_backend()
537|    cert = (
538|        x509.CertificateBuilder()
539|        .subject_name(subject)
540|        .issuer_name(subject)
541|        .public_key(pkey.public_key())
542|        .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())
543|        .not_valid_before(dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC))
544|        .not_valid_after(dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC) + dt.timedelta(days=365))
545|        .add_extension(x509.ExtendedKeyUsage([x509.OID_SERVER_AUTH]), critical=False)
546|        .add_extension(
547|            x509.SubjectAlternativeName([x509.DNSName(cn), x509.DNSName(f"*.{cn}")]),
548|            critical=False,
549|        )
550|        .sign(pkey, hashes.SHA256(), backend)
551|    )
552|    return cert, pkey
553|

555|def make_ssl_devcert(
556|    base_path: str, host: str | None = None, cn: str | None = None
557|) -> tuple[str, str]:
558|    """Creates an SSL key for development.  This should be used instead of
559|    the ``'adhoc'`` key which generates a new cert on each server start.
560|    It accepts a path for where it should store the key and cert and
561|    either a host or CN.  If a host is given it will use the CN
562|    ``*.host/CN=host``.
563|
564|    For more information see :func:`run_simple`.
565|
566|    .. versionadded:: 0.9
567|
568|    :param base_path: the path to the certificate and key.  The extension
569|                      ``.crt`` is added for the certificate, ``.key`` is
570|                      added for the key.
571|    :param host: the name of the host.  This can be used as an alternative
572|                 for the `cn`.
573|    :param cn: the `CN` to use.
574|    """
575|
576|    if host is not None:
577|        cn = host
578|    cert, pkey = generate_adhoc_ssl_pair(cn=cn)
579|
580|    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
581|
582|    cert_file = f"{base_path}.crt"
583|    pkey_file = f"{base_path}.key"
584|
585|    with open(cert_file, "wb") as f:
586|        f.write(cert.public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.PEM))
587|    with open(pkey_file, "wb") as f:
588|        f.write(
589|            pkey.private_bytes(
590|                encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
591|                format=serialization.PrivateFormat.TraditionalOpenSSL,
592|                encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),
593|            )
594|        )
595|
596|    return cert_file, pkey_file
597|

599|def generate_adhoc_ssl_context() -> ssl.SSLContext:
600|    """Generates an adhoc SSL context for the development server."""
601|    import atexit
602|    import tempfile
603|
604|    cert, pkey = generate_adhoc_ssl_pair()
605|
606|    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
607|
608|    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("wb", delete=False) as cert_file:
609|        cert_file.write(cert.public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.PEM))
610|
611|    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("wb", delete=False) as pkey_file:
612|        pkey_file.write(
613|            pkey.private_bytes(
614|                encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
615|                format=serialization.PrivateFormat.TraditionalOpenSSL,
616|                encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),
617|            )
618|        )
619|
620|    atexit.register(os.remove, cert_file.name)
621|    atexit.register(os.remove, pkey_file.name)
622|    ctx = load_ssl_context(cert_file.name, pkey_file.name)
623|    return ctx
624|

626|def load_ssl_context(
627|    cert_file: str, pkey_file: str | None = None, protocol: int | None = None
628|) -> ssl.SSLContext:
629|    """Loads SSL context from cert/private key files and optional protocol.
630|    Many parameters are directly taken from the API of
631|    :py:class:`ssl.SSLContext`.
632|
633|    :param cert_file: Path of the certificate to use.
634|    :param pkey_file: Path of the private key to use. If not given, the key
635|                      will be obtained from the certificate file.
636|    :param protocol: A ``PROTOCOL`` constant from the :mod:`ssl` module.
637|        Defaults to :data:`ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER`.
638|    """
639|    if protocol is None:
640|        protocol = ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER
641|
642|    ctx = ssl.SSLContext(protocol)
643|    ctx.load_cert_chain(cert_file, pkey_file)
644|    return ctx

654|def select_address_family(host: str, port: int) -> socket.AddressFamily:
655|    """Return ``AF_INET4``, ``AF_INET6``, or ``AF_UNIX`` depending on
656|    the host and port."""
657|    if host.startswith("unix://"):
658|        return socket.AF_UNIX
659|    elif ":" in host and hasattr(socket, "AF_INET6"):
660|        return socket.AF_INET6
661|    return socket.AF_INET

664|def get_sockaddr(
665|    host: str, port: int, family: socket.AddressFamily
666|) -> tuple[str, int] | str:
667|    """Return a fully qualified socket address that can be passed to
668|    :func:`socket.bind`."""
669|    if family == af_unix:
670|        # Absolute path avoids IDNA encoding error when path starts with dot.
671|        return os.path.abspath(host.partition("://")[2])
672|    try:
673|        res = socket.getaddrinfo(
674|            host, port, family, socket.SOCK_STREAM, socket.IPPROTO_TCP
675|        )
676|    except socket.gaierror:
677|        return host, port
678|    return res[0][4]  # type: ignore[return-value]

682|    """Get the IP address of an external interface. Used when binding to
683|    0.0.0.0 or ::1 to show a more useful URL.
684|
685|    :meta private:
686|    """
687|    # arbitrary private address
688|    host = "fd31:f903:5ab5:1::1" if family == socket.AF_INET6 else "10.253.155.219"
689|

695|
696|        return s.getsockname()[0]  # type: ignore[no-any-return]

699|class BaseWSGIServer(HTTPServer):
700|    """A WSGI server that that handles one request at a time.
701|
702|    Use :func:`make_server` to create a server instance.
703|    """
704|
705|    multithread = False
706|    multiprocess = False
707|    request_queue_size = LISTEN_QUEUE
708|    allow_reuse_address = True
709|
710|    def __init__(
711|        self,
712|        host: str,
713|        port: int,
714|        app: wt.WSGIApplication,
715|        handler: type[WSGIRequestHandler] | None = None,
716|        passthrough_errors: bool = False,
717|        ssl_context: _TSSLContextArg = None,
718|        fd: int | None = None,
719|    ) -> None:
720|        if handler is None:
721|            handler = WSGIRequestHandler
722|
723|        # If the handler doesn't directly set a protocol version and
724|        # thread or process workers are used, then allow chunked
725|        # responses and keep-alive connections by enabling HTTP/1.1.
726|        if "protocol_version" not in vars(handler) and (
727|            self.multithread or self.multiprocess
728|        ):
729|            handler.protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
730|
731|        self.host = host
732|        self.port = port
733|        self.app = app
734|        self.passthrough_errors = passthrough_errors
735|
736|        self.address_family = address_family = select_address_family(host, port)
737|        server_address = get_sockaddr(host, int(port), address_family)
738|
739|        # Remove a leftover Unix socket file from a previous run. Don't
740|        # remove a file that was set up by run_simple.
741|        if address_family == af_unix and fd is None:
742|            server_address = t.cast(str, server_address)
743|
744|            if os.path.exists(server_address):
745|                os.unlink(server_address)
746|
747|        # Bind and activate will be handled manually, it should only
748|        # happen if we're not using a socket that was already set up.
749|        super().__init__(
750|            server_address,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
751|            handler,
752|            bind_and_activate=False,
753|        )
754|
755|        if fd is None:
756|            # No existing socket descriptor, do bind_and_activate=True.
757|            try:
758|                self.server_bind()
759|                self.server_activate()
760|            except OSError as e:
761|                # Catch connection issues and show them without the traceback. Show
762|                # extra instructions for address not found, and for macOS.
763|                self.server_close()
764|                print(e.strerror, file=sys.stderr)
765|
766|                if e.errno == errno.EADDRINUSE:
767|                    print(
768|                        f"Port {port} is in use by another program. Either identify and"
769|                        " stop that program, or start the server with a different"
770|                        " port.",
771|                        file=sys.stderr,
772|                    )
773|
774|                    if sys.platform == "darwin" and port == 5000:
775|                        print(
776|                            "On macOS, try searching for and disabling"
777|                            " 'AirPlay Receiver' in System Settings.",
778|                            file=sys.stderr,
779|                        )
780|
781|                sys.exit(1)
782|            except BaseException:
783|                self.server_close()
784|                raise
785|        else:
786|            # TCPServer automatically opens a socket even if bind_and_activate is False.
787|            # Close it to silence a ResourceWarning.
788|            self.server_close()
789|
790|            # Use the passed in socket directly.
791|            self.socket = socket.fromfd(fd, address_family, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
792|            self.server_address = self.socket.getsockname()
793|
794|        if address_family != af_unix:
795|            # If port was 0, this will record the bound port.
796|            self.port = self.server_address[1]
797|
798|        if ssl_context is not None:
799|            if isinstance(ssl_context, tuple):
800|                ssl_context = load_ssl_context(*ssl_context)
801|            elif ssl_context == "adhoc":
802|                ssl_context = generate_adhoc_ssl_context()
803|
804|            self.socket = ssl_context.wrap_socket(self.socket, server_side=True)
805|            self.ssl_context: ssl.SSLContext | None = ssl_context
806|        else:
807|            self.ssl_context = None
808|
809|        import importlib.metadata
810|
811|        self._server_version = f"Werkzeug/{importlib.metadata.version('werkzeug')}"
812|

814|        _log(type, message, *args)

69|def _find_stat_paths(
70|    extra_files: set[str], exclude_patterns: set[str]
71|) -> t.Iterable[str]:
72|    """Find paths for the stat reloader to watch. Returns imported
73|    module files, Python files under non-system paths. Extra files and
74|    Python files under extra directories can also be scanned.
75|
76|    System paths have to be excluded for efficiency. Non-system paths,
77|    such as a project root or ``sys.path.insert``, should be the paths
78|    of interest to the user anyway.
79|    """
80|    paths = set()
81|
82|    for path in chain(list(sys.path), extra_files):
83|        path = os.path.abspath(path)
84|
85|        if os.path.isfile(path):
86|            # zip file on sys.path, or extra file
87|            paths.add(path)
88|            continue
89|
90|        parent_has_py = {os.path.dirname(path): True}
91|
92|        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(path):
93|            if (
94|                root.startswith(_stat_ignore_scan)
95|                or os.path.basename(root) in _ignore_common_dirs
96|            ):
97|                dirs.clear()
98|                continue
99|
100|            has_py = False
101|
102|            for name in files:
103|                if name.endswith((".py", ".pyc")):
104|                    has_py = True
105|                    paths.add(os.path.join(root, name))
106|
107|            # Optimization: stop scanning a directory if neither it nor
108|            # its parent contained Python files.
109|            if not (has_py or parent_has_py[os.path.dirname(root)]):
110|                dirs.clear()
111|                continue
112|
113|            parent_has_py[root] = has_py

115|    paths.update(_iter_module_paths())

124|    sources as the stat reloader, but watches everything under

144|def _find_common_roots(paths: t.Iterable[str]) -> t.Iterable[str]:
145|    root: dict[str, dict[str, t.Any]] = {}
146|
147|    for chunks in sorted((PurePath(x).parts for x in paths), key=len, reverse=True):
148|        node = root
149|
150|        for chunk in chunks:
151|            node = node.setdefault(chunk, {})
152|
153|        node.clear()

155|    rv = set()
156|
157|    def _walk(node: t.Mapping[str, dict[str, t.Any]], path: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
158|        for prefix, child in node.items():
159|            _walk(child, path + (prefix,))
160|
161|        # If there are no more nodes, and a path has been accumulated, add it.
162|        # Path may be empty if the "" entry is in sys.path.
163|        if not node and path:
164|            rv.add(os.path.join(*path))

166|    _walk(root, ())

260|class WatchdogReloaderLoop(ReloaderLoop):
261|    def __init__(self, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> None:
262|        from watchdog.events import EVENT_TYPE_CLOSED
263|        from watchdog.events import EVENT_TYPE_CREATED
264|        from watchdog.events import EVENT_TYPE_DELETED
265|        from watchdog.events import EVENT_TYPE_MODIFIED
266|        from watchdog.events import EVENT_TYPE_MOVED
267|        from watchdog.events import FileSystemEvent
268|        from watchdog.events import PatternMatchingEventHandler

275|            def dispatch(self, event: FileSystemEvent) -> None:
276|                if event.event_type not in {
277|                    EVENT_TYPE_CLOSED,
278|                    EVENT_TYPE_CREATED,
279|                    EVENT_TYPE_DELETED,
280|                    EVENT_TYPE_MODIFIED,
281|                    EVENT_TYPE_MOVED,
282|                }:
283|                    # skip events that don't involve changes to the file
284|                    return

286|                super().dispatch(event)
287|
288|            def on_any_event(self, event: FileSystemEvent) -> None:
289|                trigger_reload(event.src_path)

291|        reloader_name = Observer.__name__.lower()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
292|
293|        if reloader_name.endswith("observer"):
294|            reloader_name = reloader_name[:-8]
295|
296|        self.name = f"watchdog ({reloader_name})"
297|        self.observer = Observer()
298|        extra_patterns = (p for p in self.extra_files if not os.path.isdir(p))
299|        self.event_handler = EventHandler(
300|            patterns=["*.py", "*.pyc", "*.zip", *extra_patterns],
301|            ignore_patterns=[
302|                *[f"*/{d}/*" for d in _ignore_common_dirs],
303|                *self.exclude_patterns,
304|            ],
305|        )
306|        self.should_reload = threading.Event()
307|
308|    def trigger_reload(self, filename: str | bytes) -> None:
309|        # This is called inside an event handler, which means throwing
310|        # SystemExit has no effect.
311|        self.should_reload.set()
312|        self.log_reload(filename)

314|    def __enter__(self) -> ReloaderLoop:
315|        self.watches: dict[str, t.Any] = {}
316|        self.observer.start()
317|        return super().__enter__()

319|    def __exit__(
320|        self,
321|        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
322|        exc_val: BaseException | None,
323|        exc_tb: TracebackType | None,
324|    ) -> None:
325|        self.observer.stop()
326|        self.observer.join()
327|
328|    def run(self) -> None:
329|        while not self.should_reload.wait(timeout=self.interval):
330|            self.run_step()
331|
332|        sys.exit(3)

334|    def run_step(self) -> None:
335|        to_delete = set(self.watches)
336|
337|        for path in _find_watchdog_paths(self.extra_files, self.exclude_patterns):
338|            if path not in self.watches:
339|                try:
340|                    self.watches[path] = self.observer.schedule(
341|                        self.event_handler, path, recursive=True
342|                    )
343|                except OSError:
344|                    # Clear this path from list of watches. We don't want
345|                    # the same error message showing again in the next
346|                    # iteration.
347|                    self.watches[path] = None
348|
349|            to_delete.discard(path)
350|
351|        for path in to_delete:
352|            watch = self.watches.pop(path, None)
353|
354|            if watch is not None:

372|    """Ensure that echo mode is enabled. Some tools such as PDB disable
373|    it which causes usability issues after a reload."""

253|                items.append((key, self.repr(value)))
254|        if items is None:
255|            items = []
256|            repr = self.repr(obj)
257|            for key in dir(obj):
258|                try:
259|                    items.append((key, self.repr(getattr(obj, key))))
260|                except Exception:
261|                    pass
262|            title = "Details for"
263|        title += f" {object.__repr__(obj)[1:-1]}"
264|        return self.render_object_dump(items, title, repr)
265|
266|    def dump_locals(self, d: dict[str, t.Any]) -> str:
267|        items = [(key, self.repr(value)) for key, value in d.items()]
268|        return self.render_object_dump(items, "Local variables in frame")
269|
270|    def render_object_dump(
271|        self, items: list[tuple[str, str]], title: str, repr: str | None = None
272|    ) -> str:
273|        html_items = []
274|        for key, value in items:
275|            html_items.append(f"<tr><th>{escape(key)}<td><pre class=repr>{value}</pre>")

29|class SharedDataMiddleware:
30|    """Serve static files during development. Use the HTTP server in front of
31|    the application to serve static files in production.
32|
33|    Given a map of base URL paths to directories, this will match a requested
34|    file under a path to a file in a directory. Unmatched paths will be
35|    forwarded to the wrapped application.
36|
37|    - ``"/static": "static"`` matches paths under the "static" directory.
38|    - ``"/robots.txt": "generated/robots.txt"`` matches a single path and file.
39|    - ``"/toolbar": ("toolbar", "static")`` matches paths under the "static"
40|      directory within the importable "toolbar" Python package.
41|
42|    :param app: The application to use for paths not handled by the middleware.
43|        Using :exc:`.NotFound` will return 404 for any other path.
44|    :param exports: Map URL paths to a folder with static files. A ``str`` is a
45|        filesystem path to a directory or single file, relative to the current
46|        directory. A ``(package, path)`` tuple is a path within an importable
47|        Python package. URL path keys are matched in order.
48|    :param disallow: A pattern for :func:`~fnmatch.fnmatch`. If it matches the
49|        loaded filename, the file is not served.
50|    :param cache_timeout: Set the ``Cache-Control`` ``max-age`` directive. If
51|        not set, conditional caching is used, which is typically what you want.
52|
53|    .. versionchanged:: 3.2
54|        The ``cache`` and ``fallback_mimetype`` parameters are deprecated and
55|        will be removed in Werkzeug 4.0.
56|
57|        The ``cache_timeout`` parameter is disabled by default, enabling
58|        conditional caching.
59|
60|        Conditional and range requests are supported.
61|
62|    .. versionchanged:: 1.0
63|        The default ``fallback_mimetype`` is ``application/octet-stream``
64|        If a filename looks like a text mimetype, the ``utf-8`` charset
65|        is added to it.
66|
67|    .. versionadded:: 0.6
68|        Added ``fallback_mimetype``.
69|
70|    .. versionchanged:: 0.5
71|        Added ``cache_timeout``.
72|    """
73|
74|    def __init__(
75|        self,
76|        app: wt.WSGIApplication,
77|        exports: (
78|            cabc.Mapping[str, str | tuple[str, str]]
79|            | t.Iterable[tuple[str, str | tuple[str, str]]]
80|        ),
81|        disallow: str | None = None,
82|        cache: None = None,
83|        cache_timeout: int | None = None,
84|        fallback_mimetype: None = None,
85|    ) -> None:
86|        self.app = app
87|        self.exports: list[tuple[str, _TLoader]] = []
88|        self.cache = cache
89|        self.cache_timeout = cache_timeout
90|        self.fallback_mimetype = fallback_mimetype
91|
92|        if cache is not None:
93|            import warnings
94|
95|            warnings.warn(
96|                "The 'cache' parameter is deprecated and will be removed"
97|                " in Werkzeug 4.0.",
98|                DeprecationWarning,
99|                stacklevel=2,
100|            )
101|
102|        if fallback_mimetype is not None:
103|            import warnings
104|
105|            warnings.warn(
106|                "The 'fallback_mimetype' parameter is deprecated and will be"
107|                " removed in Werkzeug 4.0.",
108|                DeprecationWarning,
109|                stacklevel=2,
110|            )
111|
112|        if isinstance(exports, cabc.Mapping):
113|            exports = exports.items()
114|
115|        for key, value in exports:
116|            if isinstance(value, tuple):
117|                loader = self.get_package_loader(*value)
118|            elif isinstance(value, str):
119|                if os.path.isfile(value):
120|                    loader = self.get_file_loader(value)
121|                else:
122|                    loader = self.get_directory_loader(value)
123|            else:
124|                raise TypeError(f"unknown def {value!r}")
125|
126|            self.exports.append((key, loader))
127|
128|        if disallow is not None:
129|            self.is_allowed = lambda x: x is not None and not fnmatch(x, disallow)  # type: ignore[method-assign,assignment]
130|
131|    def is_allowed(self, filename: str | None) -> bool:
132|        """Subclasses can override this method to disallow the access to
133|        certain files.  However by providing `disallow` in the constructor
134|        this method is overwritten.
135|        """
136|        return True
137|
138|    def _opener(self, filename: str) -> _TOpener:
139|        return lambda: (
140|            open(filename, "rb"),
141|            dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(os.path.getmtime(filename), tz=dt.UTC),
142|            os.path.getsize(filename),
143|        )
144|
145|    def get_file_loader(self, filename: str) -> _TLoader:
146|        return lambda x: (os.path.basename(filename), self._opener(filename))
147|
148|    def get_package_loader(self, package: str, package_path: str) -> _TLoader:
149|        load_time = dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC)
150|        spec = importlib.util.find_spec(package)
151|        reader = spec.loader.get_resource_reader(package)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
152|
153|        def loader(
154|            path: str | None,
155|        ) -> tuple[str | None, _TOpener | None]:
156|            if path is None:
157|                return None, None
158|
159|            path = safe_join(package_path, path)
160|
161|            if path is None:
162|                return None, None
163|
164|            basename = posixpath.basename(path)
165|
166|            try:
167|                resource = reader.open_resource(path)
168|            except OSError:
169|                return None, None
170|
171|            if isinstance(resource, BytesIO):
172|                return (
173|                    basename,
174|                    lambda: (resource, load_time, len(resource.getvalue())),
175|                )
176|
177|            return (
178|                basename,
179|                lambda: (
180|                    resource,
181|                    dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(
182|                        os.path.getmtime(resource.name), tz=dt.UTC
183|                    ),
184|                    os.path.getsize(resource.name),
185|                ),
186|            )
187|
188|        return loader
189|
190|    def get_directory_loader(self, directory: str) -> _TLoader:
191|        def loader(
192|            path: str | None,
193|        ) -> tuple[str | None, _TOpener | None]:
194|            if path is not None:
195|                path = safe_join(directory, path)
196|
197|                if path is None:
198|                    return None, None
199|            else:
200|                path = directory
201|
202|            if os.path.isfile(path):
203|                return os.path.basename(path), self._opener(path)
204|
205|            return None, None
206|
207|        return loader
208|
209|    @Request.application
210|    def __call__(self, request: Request) -> wt.WSGIApplication:
211|        path = request.path
212|
213|        for search_path, loader in self.exports:
214|            if search_path == path:
215|                filename, opener = loader(None)
216|
217|                if opener is not None:
218|                    break
219|
220|            if not search_path.endswith("/"):
221|                search_path += "/"
222|
223|            if path.startswith(search_path):
224|                filename, opener = loader(path[len(search_path) :])
225|
226|                if opener is not None:
227|                    break
228|        else:
229|            return self.app
230|
231|        if not self.is_allowed(filename):
232|            return self.app
233|
234|        f, mtime, size = opener()
235|        response = send_file(
236|            f,
237|            request.environ,
238|            download_name=filename,
239|            conditional=bool(self.cache),
240|            last_modified=mtime,
241|            max_age=self.cache_timeout,
242|        )
243|
244|        if response.content_length is None:
245|            response.content_length = size
246|
247|        if (
248|            self.fallback_mimetype is not None
249|            and response.mimetype == "application/octet-stream"
250|        ):
251|            response.mimetype = self.fallback_mimetype
252|
253|        return response

21|@dataclass
22|class State:
23|    """A representation of a rule state.
24|
25|    This includes the *rules* that correspond to the state and the
26|    possible *static* and *dynamic* transitions to the next state.
27|    """
28|
29|    dynamic: list[tuple[RulePart, State]] = field(default_factory=list)
30|    rules: list[Rule] = field(default_factory=list)
31|    static: dict[str, State] = field(default_factory=dict)
32|
33|
34|class StateMachineMatcher:
35|    def __init__(self, merge_slashes: bool) -> None:
36|        self._root = State()
37|        self.merge_slashes = merge_slashes
38|
39|    def add(self, rule: Rule) -> None:
40|        state = self._root
41|        for part in rule._parts:
42|            if part.static:
43|                state.static.setdefault(part.content, State())
44|                state = state.static[part.content]
45|            else:
46|                for test_part, new_state in state.dynamic:
47|                    if test_part == part:
48|                        state = new_state
49|                        break
50|                else:
51|                    new_state = State()
52|                    state.dynamic.append((part, new_state))
53|                    state = new_state
54|
55|        for existing in state.rules:
56|            if rule.is_duplicate(existing):
57|                raise DuplicateRuleError(existing, rule)
58|
59|        state.rules.append(rule)
60|
61|    def update(self) -> None:
62|        # For every state the dynamic transitions should be sorted by
63|        # the weight of the transition
64|        state = self._root
65|
66|        def _update_state(state: State) -> None:
67|            state.dynamic.sort(key=lambda entry: entry[0].weight)
68|            for new_state in state.static.values():
69|                _update_state(new_state)
70|            for _, new_state in state.dynamic:
71|                _update_state(new_state)
72|
73|        _update_state(state)
74|
75|    def match(
76|        self, domain: str, path: str, method: str, websocket: bool
77|    ) -> tuple[Rule, t.MutableMapping[str, t.Any]]:
78|        # To match to a rule we need to start at the root state and
79|        # try to follow the transitions until we find a match, or find
80|        # there is no transition to follow.
81|
82|        have_match_for = set()
83|        websocket_mismatch = False
84|
85|        def _match(
86|            state: State, parts: list[str], values: list[str]
87|        ) -> tuple[Rule, list[str]] | None:
88|            # This function is meant to be called recursively, and will attempt
89|            # to match the head part to the state's transitions.
90|            nonlocal have_match_for, websocket_mismatch
91|
92|            # The base case is when all parts have been matched via
93|            # transitions. Hence if there is a rule with methods &
94|            # websocket that work return it and the dynamic values
95|            # extracted.
96|            if parts == []:
97|                for rule in state.rules:
98|                    if rule.methods is not None and method not in rule.methods:
99|                        have_match_for.update(rule.methods)
100|                    elif rule.websocket != websocket:
101|                        websocket_mismatch = True
102|                    else:
103|                        return rule, values
104|
105|                # Test if there is a match with this path with a
106|                # trailing slash, if so raise an exception to report
107|                # that matching is possible with an additional slash
108|                if "" in state.static:
109|                    for rule in state.static[""].rules:
110|                        if websocket == rule.websocket and (
111|                            rule.methods is None or method in rule.methods
112|                        ):
113|                            if rule.strict_slashes:
114|                                raise SlashRequired()
115|                            else:
116|                                return rule, values
117|                return None
118|
119|            part = parts[0]
120|            # To match this part try the static transitions first
121|            if part in state.static:
122|                rv = _match(state.static[part], parts[1:], values)
123|                if rv is not None:
124|                    return rv
125|            # No match via the static transitions, so try the dynamic
126|            # ones.
127|            for test_part, new_state in state.dynamic:
128|                target = part
129|                remaining = parts[1:]
130|                # A final part indicates a transition that always
131|                # consumes the remaining parts i.e. transitions to a
132|                # final state.
133|                if test_part.final:
134|                    target = "/".join(parts)
135|                    remaining = []
136|                match = re.compile(test_part.content).match(target)
137|                if match is not None:
138|                    if test_part.suffixed:
139|                        # If a part_isolating=False part has a slash suffix, remove the
140|                        # suffix from the match and check for the slash redirect next.
141|                        suffix = match.groups()[-1]
142|                        if suffix == "/":
143|                            remaining = [""]
144|
145|                    converter_groups = sorted(
146|                        (
147|                            item
148|                            for item in match.groupdict().items()
149|                            if item[0].startswith("__werkzeug_")
150|                        ),
151|                        key=lambda item: int(item[0][11:]),
152|                    )
153|                    groups = [item[1] for item in converter_groups]
154|                    rv = _match(new_state, remaining, values + groups)
155|                    if rv is not None:
156|                        return rv
157|
158|            # If there is no match and the only part left is a
159|            # trailing slash ("") consider rules that aren't
160|            # strict-slashes as these should match if there is a final
161|            # slash part.
162|            if parts == [""]:
163|                for rule in state.rules:
164|                    if rule.strict_slashes:
165|                        continue
166|                    if rule.methods is not None and method not in rule.methods:
167|                        have_match_for.update(rule.methods)
168|                    elif rule.websocket != websocket:
169|                        websocket_mismatch = True
170|                    else:
171|                        return rule, values
172|
173|            return None
174|
175|        try:
176|            rv = _match(self._root, [domain, *path.split("/")], [])
177|        except SlashRequired:
178|            raise RequestPath(f"{path}/") from None
179|
180|        if self.merge_slashes and rv is None:
181|            # Try to match again, but with slashes merged
182|            path = re.sub("/{2,}", "/", path)
183|            try:
184|                rv = _match(self._root, [domain, *path.split("/")], [])
185|            except SlashRequired:
186|                raise RequestPath(f"{path}/") from None
187|            if rv is None or rv[0].merge_slashes is False:
188|                raise NoMatch(have_match_for, websocket_mismatch)
189|            else:
190|                raise RequestPath(f"{path}")
191|        elif rv is not None:
192|            rule, values = rv
193|
194|            result = {}
195|            for name, value in zip(rule._converters.keys(), values, strict=True):
196|                try:
197|                    value = rule._converters[name].to_python(value)
198|                except ValidationError as e:
199|                    raise NoMatch(have_match_for, websocket_mismatch) from e
200|                result[str(name)] = value
201|            if rule.defaults:
202|                result.update(rule.defaults)
203|
204|            if rule.alias and rule.map.redirect_defaults:
205|                raise RequestAliasRedirect(result, rule.endpoint)
206|
207|            return rule, result
208|
209|        raise NoMatch(have_match_for, websocket_mismatch)

23|    """Convenience method for conditional requests.
24|    :param http_range: Range HTTP header
25|    :param http_if_range: If-Range HTTP header
26|    :param http_if_modified_since: If-Modified-Since HTTP header
27|    :param http_if_none_match: If-None-Match HTTP header
28|    :param http_if_match: If-Match HTTP header
29|    :param etag: the ETag for the response for comparison.
30|    :param data: or alternatively the data of the response to automatically
31|                 generate an ETag using :func:`generate_etag`.
32|    :param last_modified: an optional date of the last modification.

34|                            account.

39|        ``apply_range`` perform their own checks.

53|    # comparisons. Mark naive datetimes as UTC.

56|

59|        # https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7233#section-3.2
60|        # A server MUST ignore an If-Range header field received in a request
61|        # that does not contain a Range header field.

65|        modified_since: datetime | None = if_range.date
66|    else:
67|        modified_since = parse_date(http_if_modified_since)
68|
69|    if modified_since and last_modified and last_modified <= modified_since:
70|        unmodified = True
71|
72|    if etag:
73|        if (parsed_etag := ETag.from_header(etag)) is None:
74|            unmodified = False
75|        elif if_range is not None and if_range.etag is not None:
76|            unmodified = if_range.etag == parsed_etag.value
77|        else:
78|            # https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7232#section-3.2
79|            # "A recipient MUST use the weak comparison function when comparing

274|        class_value: t.Any | None = None,

282|            def bind_f(

286|
287|        elif f is not None:

289|
290|            def bind_f(

137|        self.headers_set = headers_set

226|class LintMiddleware:
227|    """Warns about common errors in the WSGI and HTTP behavior of the
228|    server and wrapped application. Some of the issues it checks are:
229|
230|    -   invalid status codes
231|    -   non-bytes sent to the WSGI server
232|    -   strings returned from the WSGI application
233|    -   non-empty conditional responses
234|    -   unquoted ETag values
235|    -   relative URLs in the Location header
236|    -   unsafe calls to wsgi.input
237|    -   unclosed iterators
238|
239|    Error information is emitted using the :mod:`warnings` module.
240|
241|    :param app: The WSGI application to wrap.
242|
243|    .. code-block:: python
244|
245|        from werkzeug.middleware.lint import LintMiddleware
246|        app = LintMiddleware(app)
247|    """
248|
249|    def __init__(self, app: wt.WSGIApplication) -> None:
250|        self.app = app
251|
252|    def check_environ(self, environ: wt.WSGIEnvironment) -> None:
253|        if type(environ) is not dict:  # noqa: E721
254|            warn(
255|                "WSGI environment is not a standard Python dict.",
256|                WSGIWarning,
257|                stacklevel=4,
258|            )
259|        for key in (
260|            "REQUEST_METHOD",
261|            "SERVER_NAME",
262|            "SERVER_PORT",
263|            "wsgi.version",
264|            "wsgi.input",
265|            "wsgi.errors",
266|            "wsgi.multithread",
267|            "wsgi.multiprocess",
268|            "wsgi.run_once",
269|        ):
270|            if key not in environ:
271|                warn(
272|                    f"Required environment key {key!r} not found",
273|                    WSGIWarning,
274|                    stacklevel=3,
275|                )
276|        if environ["wsgi.version"] != (1, 0):
277|            warn("Environ is not a WSGI 1.0 environ.", WSGIWarning, stacklevel=3)
278|
279|        script_name = environ.get("SCRIPT_NAME", "")
280|        path_info = environ.get("PATH_INFO", "")
281|
282|        if script_name and script_name[0] != "/":
283|            warn(
284|                f"'SCRIPT_NAME' does not start with a slash: {script_name!r}",
285|                WSGIWarning,
286|                stacklevel=3,
287|            )
288|
289|        if path_info and path_info[0] != "/":
290|            warn(
291|                f"'PATH_INFO' does not start with a slash: {path_info!r}",
292|                WSGIWarning,
293|                stacklevel=3,
294|            )
295|
296|    def check_start_response(
297|        self,
298|        status: str,
299|        headers: list[tuple[str, str]],
300|        exc_info: None | (tuple[type[BaseException], BaseException, TracebackType]),
301|    ) -> tuple[int, Headers]:
302|        check_type("status", status, str)
303|        status_code_str = status.split(None, 1)[0]
304|
305|        if len(status_code_str) != 3 or not status_code_str.isdecimal():
306|            warn("Status code must be three digits.", WSGIWarning, stacklevel=3)
307|
308|        if len(status) < 4 or status[3] != " ":
309|            warn(
310|                f"Invalid value for status {status!r}. Valid status strings are three"
311|                " digits, a space and a status explanation.",
312|                WSGIWarning,
313|                stacklevel=3,
314|            )
315|
316|        status_code = int(status_code_str)
317|
318|        if status_code < 100:
319|            warn("Status code < 100 detected.", WSGIWarning, stacklevel=3)
320|
321|        if type(headers) is not list:  # noqa: E721
322|            warn("Header list is not a list.", WSGIWarning, stacklevel=3)
323|
324|        for item in headers:
325|            if type(item) is not tuple or len(item) != 2:
326|                warn("Header items must be 2-item tuples.", WSGIWarning, stacklevel=3)
327|            name, value = item
328|            if type(name) is not str or type(value) is not str:  # noqa: E721
329|                warn(
330|                    "Header keys and values must be strings.", WSGIWarning, stacklevel=3
331|                )
332|            if name.lower() == "status":
333|                warn(
334|                    "The status header is not supported due to"
335|                    " conflicts with the CGI spec.",
336|                    WSGIWarning,
337|                    stacklevel=3,
338|                )
339|
340|        if exc_info is not None and not isinstance(exc_info, tuple):
341|            warn("Invalid value for exc_info.", WSGIWarning, stacklevel=3)
342|
343|        headers_obj = Headers(headers)
344|        self.check_headers(headers_obj)
345|
346|        return status_code, headers_obj
347|
348|    def check_headers(self, headers: Headers) -> None:
349|        etag = headers.get("ETag")
350|
351|        if etag is not None:
352|            if etag.startswith(("W/", "w/")):
353|                if etag.startswith("w/"):
354|                    warn(
355|                        "Weak ETag marker should be upper case.",
356|                        HTTPWarning,
357|                        stacklevel=4,
358|                    )
359|
360|                etag = etag[2:]
361|
362|            if not (etag[:1] == etag[-1:] == '"'):
363|                warn("Unquoted ETag emitted.", HTTPWarning, stacklevel=4)
364|
365|        location = headers.get("Location")
366|
367|        if location is not None:
368|            if not urlparse(location).netloc:
369|                warn(
370|                    "Absolute URLs required for location header.",
371|                    HTTPWarning,
372|                    stacklevel=4,
373|                )
374|
375|    def check_iterator(self, app_iter: t.Iterable[bytes]) -> None:
376|        if isinstance(app_iter, (str, bytes)):
377|            warn(
378|                "The application returned a string. The response will send one"
379|                " character at a time to the client, which will kill performance."
380|                " Return a list or iterable instead.",
381|                WSGIWarning,
382|                stacklevel=3,
383|            )
384|
385|    def __call__(self, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Iterable[bytes]:
386|        if len(args) != 2:
387|            warn("A WSGI app takes two arguments.", WSGIWarning, stacklevel=2)
388|
389|        if kwargs:
390|            warn(
391|                "A WSGI app does not take keyword arguments.", WSGIWarning, stacklevel=2
392|            )
393|
394|        environ: wt.WSGIEnvironment = args[0]
395|        start_response: wt.StartResponse = args[1]
396|
397|        self.check_environ(environ)
398|        environ["wsgi.input"] = InputStream(environ["wsgi.input"])
399|        environ["wsgi.errors"] = ErrorStream(environ["wsgi.errors"])
400|
401|        headers_set: list[t.Any] = []
402|        chunks: list[int] = []
403|
404|        def checking_start_response(
405|            *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any
406|        ) -> t.Callable[[bytes], None]:
407|            if len(args) not in {2, 3}:
408|                warn(
409|                    f"Invalid number of arguments: {len(args)}, expected 2 or 3.",
410|                    WSGIWarning,
411|                    stacklevel=2,
412|                )
413|
414|            if kwargs:
415|                warn(
416|                    "'start_response' does not take keyword arguments.",
417|                    WSGIWarning,
418|                    stacklevel=2,
419|                )
420|
421|            status: str = args[0]
422|            headers: list[tuple[str, str]] = args[1]
423|            exc_info: (
424|                None | (tuple[type[BaseException], BaseException, TracebackType])
425|            ) = args[2] if len(args) == 3 else None
426|
427|            headers_set[:] = self.check_start_response(status, headers, exc_info)
428|            return GuardedWrite(start_response(status, headers, exc_info), chunks)
429|
430|        app_iter = self.app(environ, t.cast(wt.StartResponse, checking_start_response))
431|        self.check_iterator(app_iter)
432|        return GuardedIterator(
433|            app_iter, t.cast(tuple[int, Headers], headers_set), chunks
434|        )
